allNodesLists.name: All Alone in the Night
allNodesLists.data:
Thanks to our amazing devs, you no longer have to use a command block to reload your questbook between updates. This means you'll get all new quests automatically upon updating to a new version of GTNH! Isn't that convenient?

If, for whatever reason, you want to manually reload your questbook, you can do so by typing /bq_admin default load in the chat window. You will need to be an admin for it to work, though.

Here's another questbook in case you already lost the one you spawned with. Don't forget that it can also be viewed at any time by pressing the Tilde (~) key if you have not changed its keybind.

§3Some command blocks are still used for specific tasks, but they do not concern the average player since they are admin-only and thus are not craftable.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lAll Alone in the Night
allNodesLists.tooltip:
All Alone in the Night
Prequest requests:
Crafting Time

allNodesLists.name: Backup Your Stuff...
allNodesLists.data:
The mod ServerUtilities (SU) is included in the pack to backup your world. You can adjust save path, frequency, and the number of backups to keep in its settings at '.minecraft\serverutilities\serverutilities.cfg'.

If you need to restore from a backup, you can find them in the backups folder in the instance directory.

Remember that the mods JourneyMap and Thaumcraft Node Tracker store information outside of what most solutions back up, so please backup your journeymap and tcnodetracker folders yourself.

The Thaumcraft data is a little buggy, losing scanned aspect data and Thaumonomicon data, so consider backing it up as well. The file is at 'saves\\playerdata\.thaum'.

If you move to another drive or computer, don't forget to migrate all the backed up files, not just the world folder.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lBackup Your Stuff...

allNodesLists.name: "Baked" Potatoes
allNodesLists.data: Eating raw potatoes isn't that healthy, as you might have noticed. Some potatoes are green and poisonous already. After you get a furnace you can make delicious baked potatoes as another food alternative. Put a baked potato on a stick to make it even more delicious.
allNodesLists.title: §1§l"Baked" Potatoes

allNodesLists.name: Bamboo Fence
allNodesLists.data:
Maybe you're lucky and started in a bamboo forest. Bamboo is a very useful tree since it grows really fast and when you break the bottom-most block, the whole thing comes apart.

You can use them as sticks, or you can place the bamboo sticks to grow and make a three-block-tall wall to protect your base. You can also use Berry Bushes for that, assuming you don't want to spend materials on fences.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lBamboo Fence

allNodesLists.name: Berry Medley
allNodesLists.data: Hmmm... what can you do with all those berries? Just eating? You will see that they have a very low saturation level. Let's plant the new berry bushes and mix the berries to make some better food.

allNodesLists.name: Better Questing?
allNodesLists.data:
Better Questing has a number of useful commands for the questbook (QB). You need to have cheats enabled to use them.

/bq_admin default load
Use this command to update your QB after you update the modpack. It reloads the quest database from the file. Your save file stores a version of the QB that can be different from the one in the file.

/bq_admin edit
Toggles editing quests. Pressing RMB on the quest will open a context menu to share it or copy its ID.

/bq_admin reset all
Resets all quests. Use this if you want to start over, or are editing the QB. You should specify the player as well if it is a server, otherwise you can skip that part.

/bq_admin reset
Resets a specific quest, defined by the quest ID. Sometimes it may be easier to go into Edit Mode > Designer Tool to specify what to reset.

/bq_admin complete
Completes a specific quest, similarly to the above. You can still claim the rewards. Use this command if a quest is broken, and then report it on GitHub, but please check if it's already reported.

/bq_admin default save
Saves changes to the QB after editing it.

/bq_copyquests
If you want to sync the quests with someone in your party, then use this. They won't get any rewards for that though.

/bq_admin hardcore
Enables BQ3 Hardcore Mode. You only start with 3 lives, so best of luck. Additional life hearts are available in the Kill all the Things tab.

Aside from the consume-type quests, a quest counts for everyone in the party if one person finished it. However, if someone joined your party later, you need to get them up to speed first either through /bq_copyquests above, or manually. Otherwise, your quest completion won't count for them because the requirements for that quest are not fulfilled for them.

If your singleplayer world does not have cheats enabled, go to the ESC screen, open to LAN, then enable cheats. This makes pausing impossible until you reload afterwards. If you host a server, you can run the commands in the command line, without "/". You can also edit the level.dat file, and set 'allowCommands' to 1, but make sure to backup your world before doing that.

[warn]For quests to save properly, you must be online and logged into your Mojang account when starting the game. Sorry, it's a limitation of Better Questing.[/warn]
allNodesLists.title: §1§lBetter Questing?

allNodesLists.name: Cows Are Supposed to Moo!
allNodesLists.data:
What the...? You noticed that sometimes when you kill something, even a cow or chicken, it explodes! What madness!

To stop it, use a proper GregTech Knife or Butchery Knife to kill them. Craft a flint GregTech knife with a stick and a piece of flint.

To see its recipe, see how a generic knife is made - NEI should show you many pages. The recipe you need should be on the last page. You can scroll pages with your mouse wheel.

[note]Alternatively you can use the search bar to search for a specific tool material, in this case flint![/note]

As a reward, here's an iron knife to use once the flint one wears out.

allNodesLists.name: Creeping Dread
allNodesLists.data:
Creepers can make you have a baaaad time.

Drowning Creeper - when it explodes, it surrounds you in a ball of cobble filled with water. Not only do you have to escape, but the cobble is infested with silverfish! And those silverfish are all infernal! The best way to deal with it is to first escape up or down. If you have to clear the cobble ball, first clear the water. Surrounding the cobble with a dirt moat will keep the silverfish inside and unable to hide. Put down punjis, quicksand, or lava, and/or spectral glass. Make a wall with a 1x1 window and use that to break the cobbles - fishing silverfish is especially dangerous.

Ender Creeper - Randomly teleports you a short distance - possibly deep underground.

allNodesLists.name: Even more challenges needed?
allNodesLists.data:
You have played through most of the pack a few times already? Maybe you even made a Stargate? Or are you just looking for something a bit different? Don't worry, we have a few options for you:

- Play in Hardcore. Either Minecraft Hardcore, or BetterQuesting Hardcore. The latter is a bit more forgiving. Maybe this seems impossible, but people have indeed reached UEV+ in Minecraft Hardcore. Better be prepared to restart a few times. This is obviously not for everybody.

- Never make a rocket. The so called §ono-rocket run§r is somewhat supported by now, you will be able to do almost everything in the pack. Use bees, crops, and blood magic meteors as your main resource production. Be warned though that such a challenge is grindy and slow. For instance, you might need to collect large amounts of aluminium gravel to get your first titanium. Or have to start breeding bees early without much technology to help.

- Skyblock. Yes, really. It is also known as Garden of Grind and it is absolutely brutal. There is no actually supported skyblock version of the pack but some players have figured out the minimal amount of changes needed to make it work. Ask around or search on the official discord channel for all the details. But don't expect any fun down this road.

- Speedrunning. A few players have designed some basic rules and have started to record speedruns to early game goals like the Coke Oven. Ask around or search on the official discord channel for all the details. Maybe you just want to watch how they do it.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lEven more challenges needed?

allNodesLists.name: Goals
allNodesLists.data:
GregTech New Horizons is a long and intricate mod pack with massive amounts of custom content and over three thousand quests to guide you through it.

We recommend you set yourself small goals from tier to tier and see how far your journey takes you.

The ultimate late game goal is to craft a Stargate or two, but the recipe is outrageous, and very few players have ever done so.

If you need a big goal for your run, we suggest to aim for something less crazy.
Like going to the moon if it's your first time playing.
Or making and automating an Assembly Line if you have never done so.
Or crafting the Tier 8 Rocket which is the last regular rocket and is reached in UHV.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lGoals

allNodesLists.name: Loading the Chunks
allNodesLists.data:
Minecraft works in chunks - the 16x16 columns of blocks from bedrock to sky. The chunks in a radius around you are simulated or, in other words, chunkloaded. If a chunk is not loaded, nothing happens in it - crops don't grow, machines don't work. Thus, you want to have your base chunkloaded when you're off exploring. Later on, you want your base chunkloaded so things don't spontaneously blow up, especially multi-block machines.

You can chunkload in a few ways:

1) The ServerUtilities mod. With default settings, you will not be able to chunkload. Feel free to change that in the config if you are in singleplayer (SP) or running your own server.

2) Use four types of Anchors from Railcraft, although they are not craftable until the Low Voltage (LV) tier. In SP, or a server you run, cheat in Admin Anchors to chunkload forever, for free. They're limited on servers to prevent TPS dropping from people chunkloading a base forever when they aren't even there. On the officials, you need to use Ender Fragments, Ender Pearls, or Coins to fuel them. Look at the tooltip on each for how long it will work, and in what chunkloader.

3) Use one of the blocks that chunkloads itself. If you do this on a server, expect the admins to possibly get very mad at you if it's not something you're allowed to do. Same for vanilla methods.

Don't use chicken chunks to get anchor-like blocks. It's buggy.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lLoading the Chunks

allNodesLists.name: Main Quests and Secondary Quests
allNodesLists.data:
Now that you've made it this far, you might notice how the two new quests look different.

The quest with the jagged edges is a main quest - it is linked to other main quests by a thick line. You must complete main quests to unlock the next tier and to progress in general. If you can't progress, go back to previous tiers and look for uncompleted main quests.

The other quest is an optional quest, and is not needed to unlock new tiers. However, optional quests often introduce you to useful items or processes.

What are the coins for? You can use them to purchase things in the "Coins, Coins, Coins" questbook tab - you have to scroll to the bottom once it unlocks!

In case you started in a bad biome, here's enough coins to purchase some saplings.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lMain Quests and Secondary Quests
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Main Quests and Secondary Quests
Prequest requests:
Crafting Time

allNodesLists.name: Monster Trap
allNodesLists.data:
If you're lucky enough to spawn near a sand- or rainforest biome, you can find some quicksand.

Collect a stack of it, dig a small ditch, and fill it with the quicksand to protect your "dirt base" home. Just don't fall in!
allNodesLists.title: §1§lMonster Trap

allNodesLists.name: Moron's Manual for Massacring Monsters
allNodesLists.data:
If you haven't noticed, this world is a true hellscape full of Special Mobs and Infernals around every corner. Unlike in vanilla, a player has to actually stay aware and pay attention to what they are fighting. Here are some tips.

If an infernal has Vengeance, don't shoot it with your 56-damage crossbow!

A high health infernal with regeneration is hard to kill. Even worse if it is a witch that can also heal herself. In those cases, run like hell, or bring a soul vial to capture it and throw it into Mount Doom.

Watch out for zombies with fishing poles - they can pull you to them. And zombies with a bow and arrow - they can shoot you back!
allNodesLists.title: §1§lMoron's Manual for Massacring Monsters
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Moron's Manual for Massacring Monsters
Prequest requests:
Sharpness: Over... 5...

allNodesLists.name: Mushroom Biomes? Why Are There So Many?
allNodesLists.data:
The GTNH pack is made for the Realistic World Generator (RWG).

If your setup uses the vanilla-biomes worldgen, you will get huge Mushroom biomes over the map. If you have this problem, please generate a new world with the RWG.

If you met this problem on a server, put "level-type=rwg" into the server.properties file and generate a new world.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lMushroom Biomes? Why Are There So Many?
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Mushroom Biomes? Why Are There So Many?
Prequest requests:
Your First Night

allNodesLists.name: Numbers in the Corner?
allNodesLists.data:
What's with the numbers in the corner? That is the In-Game Info (IGI) mod. Some of the info it gives is useful right away, some of it shines later on in progression.

For now, the most important thing it does is showing if you are in an ore chunk. Further quests will explain what it means.

If you want to hide it, type "/igi disable" in the chat. Type "/igi enable" if you want to turn it back on.

The command "/igi config" opens the configuration window to control its position, scale, and size.

The command "/xu_tps" from the mod Extra Utilities toggles numbers to measure ticktime in milliseconds and the TPS (Ticks Per Second). TPS is a measure of how well your server is running. The ideal TPS is 20.00 (meaning a ticktime of at most 50.00). If your TPS is less than 15, things are going to start lagging noticeably. At 10 or less TPS, it is going to be hard to play.
The tooltip shows three types of measurement: instantaneous, average, and worst-case. Each one first shows the ticktime and then the TPS in brackets.

If you need suggestions on solving TPS problems, feel free to ask for help in the GTNH Discord.

While GTNH comes with recommended default settings, in particular when it comes to balance, there are many commands and configurations to customize your experience. They range from accessability or debug tools to visual customization all the way to various cheats. You can find a small overview on [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Commands_and_Configurations[/url].
allNodesLists.title: §1§lNumbers in the Corner?
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Numbers in the Corner?
Prequest requests:
Your First Night

allNodesLists.name: Oak Trees Are Not Apple Trees
allNodesLists.data:
Oak trees that give apples? Who the hell added this to minecraft?
You found a way of combining an oak sapling and an apple to get an apple tree sapling. Try to plant one to get a permanent source of food.

Once you complete this quest, check out the rest of the Quest Tabs. A new one, "Coins, Coins, Coins", has unlocked. You'll want to look through all the quest tabs to make sure something new hasn't unlocked somewhere else occasionally. There are lots of tabs, so be sure to scroll down!
allNodesLists.title: §1§lOak Trees Are Not Apple Trees
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Oak Trees Are Not Apple Trees
Prequest requests:
Main Quests and Secondary Quests

allNodesLists.name: Porkchops With Attitude
allNodesLists.data: The only zombie pigman to watch out for is the Vampire Pigman. He hardly takes any damage unless you use a wooden sword as a stake, or have a magical sword.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lPorkchops With Attitude
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Porkchops With Attitude
Prequest requests:
Caught in the Web

allNodesLists.name: Rest in Pieces
allNodesLists.data: It's GLOPPing time! Go kill some pigs to gather meat. If you kill them with flint tool, they will drop cooked porkchops. Now isn't that useful!
allNodesLists.title: §1§lRest in Pieces

allNodesLists.name: Sharpness: Over... 5...
allNodesLists.data:
It's about time to craft something more useful: A sword!

Now that you have a sword, you will get credit for monster kills in the Kill All the Things tab. Watch out, monsters in this world will chew you up and spit you out!

You can find additional weapon quests on the Getting Around tab.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lSharpness: Over... 5...

allNodesLists.name: Shields UP
allNodesLists.data: With a sword in one hand, what can you do with the other? Right, you need a shield. Let's make one.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lShields UP

allNodesLists.name: Shield Update
allNodesLists.data: Your wooden shield is very weak. So you should make a better one. Looks like you need some leather, so go and find some cows.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lShield Update

allNodesLists.name: Soft Mallet Adventure
allNodesLists.data:
You now have some melon slices or pumpkins but what can you do with them?

You can just eat them or... use a mallet to get some seeds. OK, let's craft one. Perhaps you can use this mallet for some other things too.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lSoft Mallet Adventure

allNodesLists.name: SO...TIRED...MUST...SLEEP...
allNodesLists.data:
Sleepy time, and the end of the tutorial.

Congratulations! You've built your first hideout, and you should have a steady supply of food by now.

See you again in Tier 0!
allNodesLists.title: §1§lSO...TIRED...MUST...SLEEP...

allNodesLists.name: Staying Cool in the Heat
allNodesLists.data: If you happen to be near a snowy biome, you can harvest the snow to make delicious smoothies. They are more satiating than eating the berries by themselves.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lStaying Cool in the Heat
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Staying Cool in the Heat
Prequest requests:
Collecting Some Berries
Soft Mallet Adventure

allNodesLists.name: Sticks 'n Stones
allNodesLists.data:
This book has a built-in reading light, lucky you! You can read about quests while you're waiting for the night to be over, but for now, you may want to get the basics done. If it isn't dark already, go out and collect some gravel and wood.

Keep in mind that you need food, so look for Pam's Harvestcraft gardens. Save some of the drops from them for seeds. Alternatively, right-click the gardens with an empty hand to get the garden item itself. If you place it somewhere else, it will spread into more of the same garden up to a limit within that area.

Make sure to read the info-quests linked to the first quest, they have important info!
allNodesLists.title: §1§lSticks 'n Stones

allNodesLists.name: Storage For Days
allNodesLists.data:
Now that you've gotten your tools and are about to go collect a bunch of stuff, it's time to make some storage for it.
Take some of your wood, and craft a chest. You will need 4 wood, 4 planks, and 1 flint.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lStorage For Days

allNodesLists.name: Tell Me When We Reach 20
allNodesLists.data:
Jumping all the time is exhausting and makes you really hungry.
To reduce your food depletion, you might want to use stairs instead.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lTell Me When We Reach 20

allNodesLists.name: Tools
allNodesLists.data:
Now that you've got a shelter and a crafting table, you should make some tools, unless you'd like to continue punching trees with your bare hands.

You should probably make the shovel first so you can get gravel for the rest more easily.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lTools

allNodesLists.name: What's That...?
allNodesLists.data:
You've seen a lot of trees, but there are a few that look really special. You are sure that these trees are much more than just wood to build your home with or used to get charcoal. You're sure that these will be Very Important soon™.

The best place to find them is in a Magical Forest, but if you can't find one, you can try a Garden or Cherry Wood Grove. Or just randomly everywhere.

If you have trouble finding them, you can go to the Coins tab and buy them.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lWhat's That...?

allNodesLists.name: ...What You Sow
allNodesLists.data:
If you, by chance, did read the previous quest and planted the carrots, then you're fine.

Meanwhile, you should turn some more fruits and vegetables into seeds, and increase the size of your farm to get a steady supply of food.
allNodesLists.title: §1§l...What You Sow

allNodesLists.name: Where's the Flint?
allNodesLists.data:
As you might have noticed when collecting gravel, no Flint dropped for you.

Well, there is a... recipe for that. Look up Flint in Not Enough Items (NEI) and craft some!

The search field of NEI is at the bottom of the screen when you open your inventory. The results are on the right side.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lWhere's the Flint?

allNodesLists.name: You Reap...
allNodesLists.data:
You won't always get food rewards from the quests, so it might be a good idea to take care of that problem.

As you've crafted a hoe already, go and find some water nearby to make a field. With this modpack you can only make farmland within range of water. Let's trade some sticks for a carrot, so you can start your own farm.

To get other wheat, use a hoe on grass away from water. You'll get Witchery seeds too - save those for later.

Start planting a Cotton field because it's a key early-game resource.

You can also get seeds from villages, and grow the seeds from the Pam's garden food.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lYou Reap...

allNodesLists.name: Your First 'Long Range' Weapon
allNodesLists.data:
You can't make a vanilla bow or Tinkers weapons yet, but you can make a spear!

Some monsters will become much easier to kill with this long-range weapon.
allNodesLists.title: §1§lYour First 'Long Range' Weapon

allNodesLists.name: Your First Night
allNodesLists.data:
Hello, friend, and welcome to GTNH!

Don't get used to things being nice and comfy, because in about ten minutes the sun will set, and unlike Vanilla Minecraft, there's no light whatsoever at night but plenty of Infernal mobs coming to get you. So your first task is to find food and shelter for the night.

But by the end of this questtab you will have a bed to make things easier.

You don't need to keep this book. Even if you don't have the item, you can press Tilde (~) to view it at any time...unless you decided to change the keybind.

If you need any extra help or just want to hang out, feel free to visit our Discord server at [url]https://discord.gg/gtnh[/url]. And yes, the links are clickable! On the discord, select your tech tier in #role-select - it will help people to tailor their advice to your situation.

Many GTNH topics are explained in our Wiki at [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Main_Page[/url]. It does not have the same extent and structure as the Questbook, but some things are much better with pictures and tables! The wiki also has tips on extra topics like what additional mods might work with the pack, how GTNH can be installed for modern Java versions or how to set up a server.

Additionally, there is a spreadsheet at [url]https://www.gtnewhorizons.com/spreadsheet[/url] for the info you would want a spreadsheet for.

If you play through a launcher that relies on [warn]CurseForge[/warn], be aware that it doesn't always work properly. It doesn't play well with all the custom versions of mods that this pack has. So if you have any problems, first switch to another launcher like MultiMC, Prism, or Technic. The wiki has instructions there as well. The latest version of the pack is available on the Discord channel from #announcements or with the !download command.

Hopefully you didn't get munched by a monster while reading this, good luck!
allNodesLists.title: §d§3§2§1§lYour First Night

allNodesLists.name: A Better Crafting Table
allNodesLists.data:
Tired of your stuff falling out of your crafting table every time you walk away? This fancy table from Tinker's Construct has slots to hold the items in your recipe.

You can also use it to upgrade tools with 8 modifiers at a time. Very handy for Redstone additional speed and Lapis looting!

When it's placed next to a vanilla chest, it will even show the chest's inventory in the crafting window. Single or double vanilla chests only, please.

Cut it again for a sleek, low profile version.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lA Better Crafting Table

allNodesLists.name: A Better Lunch Bag
allNodesLists.data: Your lunch bag is now abused and rather old so it's time to get something better. Let's craft a lunch box which can hold way more food.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lA Better Lunch Bag

allNodesLists.name: All the Finest Cuts of Meat
allNodesLists.data:
This knife is not going to work for slaughtering the hundreds of animals you will need for food and materials. Make yourself a GregTech Butchery Knife. It stops the explosions, and kills the cows much faster, not to mention has Looting on it. Later when you get Stainless Steel, you can make a new one that will kill cows in one hit.

Note that the GT Tool damage is based on tinkers mining level.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lAll the Finest Cuts of Meat
allNodesLists.tooltip:
All the Finest Cuts of Meat
Prequest requests:
Sheep Hairdresser

allNodesLists.name: Aluminini...um...?
allNodesLists.data:
However it is spelled, you will need it. You can find it in chunks of gravel on the surface.

Use as little as possible and save the rest for when you get a macerator in Steam age, you'll get twice as much.

If you can't find any, you can get aluminum oreberries to plant from quest rewards, or you can buy them in the Coins tab.

If you get enough and fully process it, you can also get rutile for titanium out of it. Get a block of that, and you can grow the Titania crop so you can make more out of UUM. The no-rocket run starts here!
allNodesLists.title: §2§lAluminini...um...?

allNodesLists.name: Animal Farms
allNodesLists.data:
Trying to get some leather or wool? You'd probably need to spend a lot of time hunting animals and traveling around, or you could simply make a farm to get a decent amount of leather, wool, and meat close to home. Make sure you don't put too many animals in the pen or they will overcrowd and kill each other. This happens to villagers as well.

Animals will prioritize moving towards grass blocks over any other blocks, and if there's no grass blocks around, they prefer lit blocks over dark blocks. You can encourage animals to stay in pens, or at least not crowd the edges, by removing grass from around both sides of the fence and under it, and by placing a torch in the center of the pen. For sheep that need the grass to eat, which reduces time to mature and replaces sheared wool instantly, place it in the center of a cleared out area with a border of non-grass.

Also, large quantities can cause server lag, especially if they are bumping into each other a lot. So if you are in multiplayer, make sure you limit animals to no more than roughly one per block for small entities like chickens and one per two blocks for large entities like cows.

As an alternative, most animal and mob drops can be obtained from less laggy IC2 crop farms.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lAnimal Farms
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Animal Farms
Prequest requests:
Gardener
All the Finest Cuts of Meat

allNodesLists.name: Another Fuel Source
allNodesLists.data:
Lignite and regular coal are the fuel sources you'll definitely need. The latter can be turned into coal coke, which is a superior fuel source to smelt your first large batch of ore.

Lignite you can toss in a boiler once you have one.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lAnother Fuel Source

allNodesLists.name: A Quicker Way to Get Around
allNodesLists.data:
Are you ready for a longer trip? With your new lunch box, saddle, lead and of course a horse, we can start a small journey. Be sure to make paths over water, horses don't like going through deep water. If you get unseated in deep water, you can try getting on repeatedly and moving a small distance each time, this may be faster for small rivers. You can also try jumping over the deep parts if it isn't that big.

If you are playing single player or a local server, horses make a great way to get around. On non-local servers they can cause problems and desync if you have poor internet, or if the server doesn't have good TPS. Like all the official servers.

You can tie the lead to your horse and the fence to get it to stick around while you investigate something.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lA Quicker Way to Get Around
allNodesLists.tooltip:
A Quicker Way to Get Around
Prequest requests:
Tanned Leather

allNodesLists.name: Around and Around She Goes...
allNodesLists.data: ...But she'll never stop because you'll always have something to grind. You can use a hopper to keep the windmill full of items to process. Just remember to retrieve them from the dispensers.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lAround and Around She Goes...
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Around and Around She Goes...
Prequest requests:
Stick a Finger in the Air

allNodesLists.name: Basic Processing
allNodesLists.data: Most things are unavailable at the moment, so let's begin with something simple. Take some of your cobblestone and smelt it into regular stone. Since this modpack is evil, you'll need to use wood for that. How much fun is that?!
allNodesLists.title: §2§lBasic Processing

allNodesLists.name: Better Storage
allNodesLists.data: While standard chests are good for your basic items and goods, they are not ideal for storing a large amount of ore. You should build yourself some barrels in order to keep things organized.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lBetter Storage

allNodesLists.name: Better Than Barrels
allNodesLists.data:
While barrels offer a slot for a single item, drawers can have up to 4 slots each, holding 16 stacks per slot.

However, they do come with some downsides. You won't be able to make them point up or down, and you can only access the contents from the front. The automation can use any side.
allNodesLists.title: §1§2§lBetter Than Barrels

allNodesLists.name: Book Parts
allNodesLists.data: After you found a way to move water around, you had another brilliant idea: Paper! Paper is no longer made with sugarcane, you'll need wood pulp instead. You'll need a lot of wood to craft wood pulp, so better grab your axe and go chop some trees.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lBook Parts

allNodesLists.name: Bronze Javelin
allNodesLists.data: The bronze javelin is a bit expensive and has only 7 throws, yet it is a good mid-range weapon. With one bronze ingot you can replenish your stack of javelins.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lBronze Javelin
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Bronze Javelin
Prequest requests:
Making Better Tools
You Are Now Prepared, Hopefully!

allNodesLists.name: Chad - A Better Way to Make Paper
allNodesLists.data: Making paper out of wood pulp and water can be tedious and difficult. Why not use a mortar to grind the sugar cane into chad and press it with two stone slabs to paper? Later on you can use the chemical bath for a even better ratio.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lChad - A Better Way to Make Paper
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Chad - A Better Way to Make Paper
Prequest requests:
Important Tools

allNodesLists.name: Circle Shapes Give Me Comfort
allNodesLists.data:
To build a Windmill you will need a Dispenser, but that item is locked behind the next Tier. Go and find one in a Witchery Circle. They look like small versions of Stonehenge.

Look for the main quest in Multiblock Goals.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lCircle Shapes Give Me Comfort
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Circle Shapes Give Me Comfort
Prequest requests:
Important Tools

allNodesLists.name: Clay: The Gathering
allNodesLists.data: While bored, you thought that it might be a good idea to take up pottery. You should go and find some clay, the riverbanks should have some.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lClay: The Gathering

allNodesLists.name: Compact Drawers
allNodesLists.data: They are very compact and add some fanciness to your glorious dirt base.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lCompact Drawers

allNodesLists.name: Compact Storage
allNodesLists.data:
Now that you are starting to find more and more copper, you feel your wood chests are too small to hold all the stuff.

[note]It's time to upgrade your wooden chests to copper chests! Higher tiers of chests can be upgraded cheaply by using upgrade items, but not all tier chests can be upgraded directly this way. try the "Wood to Copper Chest Upgrade", upgrade from wood to a tiered chest will not be chaper.[/note]

[note]Upgraded chests cannot be connected into double chests.[/note]
allNodesLists.title: §2§lCompact Storage

allNodesLists.name: Copper
allNodesLists.data: Copper ingots can be created by smelting copper, chalcopyrite, or malachite ore.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lCopper

allNodesLists.name: Copper Ore
allNodesLists.data:
Can be found between Y 5-60 either as "Copper Ore" or "Chalcopyrite". Most of the time you'll find it together with "Iron" and "Pyrite".

To see where an ore can be found, click the raw ore in NEI, and it will show you more details. Works with small ores too.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lCopper Ore

allNodesLists.name: Copper Sky, Iron Curtain
allNodesLists.data: With your newly acquired fuel source, you are now ready to process more advanced materials than stone or clay; Iron or Copper, for example. Just in case you don't know, they spawn in rather large veins. Use the following quests to locate the most important veins.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lCopper Sky, Iron Curtain
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Copper Sky, Iron Curtain
Prequest requests:
Finally, Some Powerful Fuel

allNodesLists.name: Cotton, Cotton and More Cotton
allNodesLists.data: You've found out that cotton is very useful, it can be used to make string, wool, and some other useful items too. Make a small cotton plantation to get tons of it.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lCotton, Cotton and More Cotton
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Cotton, Cotton and More Cotton
Prequest requests:
Cow Tipper

allNodesLists.name: Cow Tipper
allNodesLists.data: Before you had to kill some pigs and sheep to complete quests. Now it's time to kill some cows and hopefully get some leather. If you are lucky and get a cow trophy you may never need to kill another cow in the future.
allNodesLists.title: §2§r§2§lCow Tipper

allNodesLists.name: Creosote
allNodesLists.data:
I guess you already turned some wood into charcoal and wonder what to do with all this creosote? Well, you can burn it in a normal Furnace to cook your food or anything else, or you can make some torches with it. You can save up on the Coal variants, while at the same time keeping the Coke Oven running for the items you really need.

You can use a Bucket to pick up the Creosote, but not a Clay Bucket, either through the icon in the machine's interface, or by right-clicking the Coke Oven with an empty bucket in hand.

You will eventually want to automate Coke Ovens, and that's when you can use it to generate power. This is mostly LV content, but the singleblock option is the GT++ Semifluid Generator, whereas the multiblock option is the Railcraft Liquid Fueled Boiler. You'll unlock the quests for these when the time comes.
allNodesLists.title: §l§2§lCreosote

allNodesLists.name: Digging Deeper
allNodesLists.data:
Now that you know what an Ore Chunk is, dig all the way down to bedrock to find if there is a vein located in it.

Check out an ore in NEI to see where you can find a vein that contains it. Search for it and click on it to get this info, among other things.

There are many types of ores, even just for getting one material like Iron, so don't stick to only one ore.

You can also search small ores in NEI, but not all of them are used.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lDigging Deeper
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Digging Deeper
Prequest requests:
How the Heck Do I Find Ores?

allNodesLists.name: Divine Rod of the Gods?
allNodesLists.data:
The Ore Finder Wand reduces the tedium of locating needed veins. If you're not sure how to craft Magnetic Iron Rod for it, check its Shapeless Crafting tab in NEI.

Once you put an ore sample into the wand, it will tell you if this ore is nearby. When you get close to the target, you will hear the sound, and the wand will tilt down to the point of being upside-down if there's a lot of target ore nearby.

Use NEI to figure out which ore is the best for your search. If you don't have the needed ore, some basic ones can be purchased in the Coins tab.

Open the wand's inventory with Shift+RMB when looking at the ground. Put the sample ore into the slot.
The rod has a 60-block range both up and down, so it can miss a vein that is located very low or if you are above the sea level.

The rod appears to work based on the GT's Material system, so anything of the same material will work.
That includes crushed ores, dusts, ingots, gems, rods, you name it. For things that don't belong to a particular Material, the rod appears to search only for that exact block - for instance, you won't detect a small ores with the usual ore block.

If the detected ore is a part of a vein, you will see a discovery message in the chat, and the vein will be automatically logged into the visual prospecting tab of your journey map.

The wand also works from inventory and hotbar, so you don't need to be actively holding it, but you get style points if you do.

The ore in the wand is stored with the player, not the wand. In other words, remove the ore if you want to give the wand to your teammate.

The Ore Finder Wand doesn't work in space! The vast cosmic energies of the sun interfere with its inner workings! Or the devs want you to use something more complicated than a stick. You choose.
allNodesLists.title: §2§e§k§l§r§3§2§lDivine Rod of the Gods?
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Divine Rod of the Gods?
Prequest requests:
Important Tools

allNodesLists.name: Don't Burn Your Fingers!
allNodesLists.data:
You have decided it's time to make some tasty pizza, but your fingers got burned badly. Reading an ancient cookbook you discovered a pair of magical items that would allow you to carry anything hot, even lava in a bucket.

§6§5The gloves have to be placed in the Baubles ring slots of Thaumcraft. You also have to place each in the correct slot, you'll get a notification if it's wrong.

§rFor the protection effect, the hot item has to be in your active slot. I wonder if there is some way to carry more than a few buckets at a time?
allNodesLists.title: §2§lDon't Burn Your Fingers!
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Don't Burn Your Fingers!
Prequest requests:
Cotton, Cotton and More Cotton

allNodesLists.name: Even More Compact Storage
allNodesLists.data:
If you found enough gold, you can upgrade your chest to make it an even bigger inventory of 9x9.

[note]Do you have iron chests that are too small? You can also upgrade with a fitting upgrade item.[/note]
allNodesLists.title: §2§lEven More Compact Storage

allNodesLists.name: Fallen From the Sky
allNodesLists.data:
You may have noticed big meteors everywhere, and maybe wondered if they're useful somehow? Well, they are, but not just yet. I'll give you a reward for collecting some now.

Inside the meteor you can find a skystone chest containing some processor press plates. Save them for later, you can't do AE2 without them. Though you can also just make them yourself in EV. Plus the chest is nice, and can be placed underneath blocks and still opened.

If all surface meteors have been raided, put some skystone in your Ore Finder to find underground ones, or wait until you can make a Meteorite Compass to find them.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lFallen From the Sky
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Fallen From the Sky
Prequest requests:
Making Better Tools

allNodesLists.name: Finally, Some Powerful Fuel
allNodesLists.data: Now that you have a coke oven, you can start producing charcoal. The more, the better. Creosote is produced at the same time, and the Coke Oven will stop when it's full with either one, which means you can't just leave the Creosote there. Refer to the Creosote quest from before to learn what to do with it.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lFinally, Some Powerful Fuel

allNodesLists.name: Finite Water!?
allNodesLists.data:
Finite water is a problem, that's for sure. Last night, you had an idea. If you can drink cacti, you should also be able make water out of 8 cacti and use that for most recipes that require water. How cool is that? So what about another trade? 10 wood for... 3 cacti so you can setup a farm. Deal?

To automate the farm, place a string next to the cactus and a sand on top of the string. Now when the cactus grows, it will automatically break! You can stack this horizontally and vertically to make a very efficient cactus farm. Use water to redirect the cactus to a convenient pickup location or to above a hopper.

First player to make a base running off of only cactus water gets a cape!
allNodesLists.title: §2§lFinite Water!?

allNodesLists.name: Forming Press v0.1
allNodesLists.data:
As you may have noticed, you cannot turn clay into bricks directly. Well, to be fair, it wasn't a good recipe anyway. You'll probably end up with something bread-shaped.

In order to make bricks, you need a form. Get yourself a knife by putting flint above a stick on the crafting grid. With a knife, you can cut a brick sized piece out and craft a blank pattern. It's as easy as that.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lForming Press v0.1

allNodesLists.name: Framing Drawers
allNodesLists.data: Now you can really make some swaggy and §oeven fancier§r drawers by using this table, all you have to do is place some decorative blocks and it will take their texture, the TOP left is the outer square, bottom left is for the front face, and top right is for the borders. This table works with almost all decorative blocks.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lFraming Drawers

allNodesLists.name: Gardener
allNodesLists.data:
If you were wondering: Why do I never get seeds when destroying grass? Because.

Use your new mattock on the grass blocks that do not have water anywhere nearby to find some seeds.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lGardener

allNodesLists.name: Getting (Char)coal
allNodesLists.data:
Now you can make the bricks for your first multiblock structure. 104 bricks to be exact. Good that you just collected a lot of resources! What a coincidence...

The bricks you'll need are somewhat special. Make sure to craft the correct ones. With that done, let's build a coke oven to get some charcoal or coal coke! It may be useful to note that the oven doesn't automatically output its fluid contents. Faucets and pumps can help to change that.
allNodesLists.title: §1§2§lGetting (Char)coal

allNodesLists.name: Getting Iron
allNodesLists.data:
Iron can be found in multiple veins.
Magnetite veins (Y 30-180), Chalcopyrite veins (Y 5-60), and Limonite veins (Y 10-40) all contain iron ore.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lGetting Iron

allNodesLists.name: Got a Flat Tire?
allNodesLists.data:
The crowbar is the GT tool used to remove a cover off of a machine, pipe, or wire. Covers can be decorative, functional like pumps and conveyors, or for safety, like putting a wooden plank over your steam pipes so they don't burn you.

Sorry, it only comes in blue!

Yes, we know there are also red crowbars, but they are from Railcraft and generally inferior. Better ignore them.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lGot a Flat Tire?

allNodesLists.name: Gravel: The Gathering
allNodesLists.data: Your tools will eventually lose durability. You think it would be a good idea to collect more gravel in order to provide yourself with flint for more tools. Try searching near water.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lGravel: The Gathering

allNodesLists.name: GT6-Styled Pipes
allNodesLists.data:
Wondering why new pipes don't always auto-connect? This was changed to make the pipes smarter. You can now use a wrench to connect only the pipes you want. You don't need a plate or a foil to prevent pipes from connecting anymore. The pipes will still autoconnect if you build one onto the other.

Pipes transferring anything hotter than a certain amount, like steam, will cause damage to a player touching them. You might want to cover hot pipes to prevent getting hurt. Also, if the heat level is higher than the pipe's heat capacity, it will melt.

Pressing RMB on a pipe in the center of the 'grid' will enable or disable a connection. It will have an X through it if the connection is enabled. You can do the same to any of the 4 corners to adjust the opposite side. You can similarly connect each of the 4 sides by clicking on the closest box in the grid.

Pipes have a free built-in shutter to reduce sloshing. Shift-RMB with a wrench on the side you want prevent input.

Pipes attempt to transfer half of their capacity twice per second, so the full capacity per second in total.

Large or Huge fluid pipes can be a poor man's storage tank, holding large amounts on their own.

For machine outputs, including the boilers and Railcraft water tanks - the one made of Water Tank Siding - you will not need pumps. Other tanks will need pumps or Tinker's Construct faucets to move fluids.

You can put covers such as GT oak planks or plates on a pipe as well. Normally this prevents connections in that direction, but you can use a screwdriver to enable connections. This lets you make pipes that look nice going through walls. Use a crowbar to remove covers.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lGT6-Styled Pipes

allNodesLists.name: How the Heck Do I Find Ores?
allNodesLists.data:
GregTech ore generation is based on veins. Veins have a fixed height and a rectangular base.

There is a vein every 3 chunks in x and z direction. The veins typically extend into the neighboring chunks and have varying forms. The center point however is very regular. It is based on the chunk number. Look at upper left of the screen to find the chunk number. This info is displayed by InGame Info XML mod. For now, you need to see chunk info like "Chunk X: 3 Z: -2".

The 3,-2 is the chunk's address. The orecenters are located at chunk numbers of the form 3N+1 for both x and z. So, 4,7 is an orecenter, as well as 10,16, -23,19, and so on. If you are in the right spot InGame Info will also say that "This is an ore chunk.".

Another useful tool is the NEI ore vein overlay which you activate by pressing F9 three times. It shows the 3x3 areas and marks the center blue.

The generation of Ore Chunks is not related to biomes.

For reading all the way, here's some iron.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lHow the Heck Do I Find Ores?
allNodesLists.tooltip:
How the Heck Do I Find Ores?
Prequest requests:
Copper Sky, Iron Curtain

allNodesLists.name: How to Open Your Wooden Doors?
allNodesLists.data:
Wooden doors make your House safer. Let's craft some wooden Pressure plates and Buttons to open these Doors.

Doors will open when they receive a redstone signal, and close again after it stops. If you place the plates on either side of a door, it will open when you step on it. Or a monster does. Double doors will open together.

You'll need to use Oak for this quest. Purchase some saplings from the Coins tab if you don't have any nearby.

Pressure plates will send a RS when an entity is on top of them. There are different types, like items or not, or mobs/player/any entity/etc.

Buttons will emit one for about 2 seconds before resetting.

Levers will emit a signal until switched back off.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lHow to Open Your Wooden Doors?
allNodesLists.tooltip:
How to Open Your Wooden Doors?

allNodesLists.name: Important Tools
allNodesLists.data:
In order to craft even basic machines, you'll need new tools. Most of them can be replaced by machines later. For now, you should become familiar with each of their recipes, as you will need a lot of these tools, starting today.

Your new tools can also be used to make Railcraft water tanks, a very useful multiblock considering the finite water feature.

There are also electric versions of the tools, you can upgrade later if you want. Also, there are many versions of the tools, they generally follow the same rules as tinkers parts in terms of how good they are, similarly to turbines. You can look at the spreadsheet for more info on GT tool stats.

For this quest, you can use whatever materials you want. The gem version of the saw is crafted differently to metal versions. Higher tier tools need steel or tungstensteel rods instead of sticks.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lImportant Tools

allNodesLists.name: Iron Ore
allNodesLists.data:
With iron tools, you are able to mine most of the Overworld ores. You've probably already found iron or magnetite, given how common it is. So bring me some ores and make some iron ingots out of them.

To see where an ore can be found, click the raw ore in NEI, and it will show you more details. Works with small ores too.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lIron Ore

allNodesLists.name: Loot Games
allNodesLists.data:
It looks like you've found a secret room hidden...not so deep within the earth. Pretty close to the surface, actually. You can find these all over the place, and have a chance at sweet sweet loot if you're good at simon says. It counts the highest level you completed, so you can fail the other rounds on purpose to go faster if you don't think you can do better. BTW, cheaters go to minecraft hell, where all the blocks have hardness -1.

If you fail with Minesweeper, it blows up. Be sure to make room for escape!

Make sure that no water or oil is flowing into the room because of worldgen, or it will kill you and destroy your grave because of 'cheating'. This is a bug.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lLoot Games

allNodesLists.name: Macerator v0.1 Alpha
allNodesLists.data:
This fancy little device works (almost...) like a macerator. Some people say it's even better, since it does not require power, yay! You only need to craft one for this quest, but you probably should make some more if you can...

[note]The mortar lets you make flint much, much more efficiently - you only need one gravel instead of three. Many tools and stations you'll make in the future will also open up better crafting recipes for things you can already make as well. If you need something but are hard up on resources, use NEI to check the recipes for that item - you may have options you didn't before.[/note]
allNodesLists.title: §1§2§lMacerator v0.1 Alpha

allNodesLists.name: Making a Better Sword
allNodesLists.data: Now it's time to make your first tinkers sword. First you have to make a blade, a type of guard, and tool rod cast forms. Melt some bronze in the smeltery and cast your tool parts. Tadaa... your first tinkers sword. There are 4 types of guard, changing them gets you a different sword type, see the tinker's book for details.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lMaking a Better Sword

allNodesLists.name: Making Better Tools
allNodesLists.data:
With aluminium and copper, you can create a material with a higher melting temperature - Aluminum Brass - which can be used to cast better tools.

For that, you need a smeltery. See the Multiblock Goals tab for details. You can also grab some extra blocks from some villages, but they don't count towards the quest.

Alternatively, there are also one-time-use clay casts available.

You can then use your fancy bronze to make better tools with a higher mining level.

Remember, you need to use the pickaxe a bit to gather mining XP if you want the full mining level on your bronze pickaxe. Certain tool upgrades can give that directly if you have an upgrade slot available.

allNodesLists.data: Now that you've found copper and tin, you should make yourself some bronze. Use your macer... mortar to grind up some copper and tin ingots, and mix them together!

allNodesLists.name: Malachite
allNodesLists.data:
Another copper source is "malachite" which can be found between Y 10-40. This vein contains more iron ore variants like "brown limonite", "yellow limonite" and "banded iron ore".

To see where an ore can be found, click the raw ore in NEI, and it will show you more details. Works with small ores too.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lMalachite

allNodesLists.name: More Compact Storage
allNodesLists.data:
Now that you are starting to find more and more iron, you feel your copper chests are too small to hold all the stuff.

[note]Do you have copper chests that are too small? You can also upgrade with a fitting upgrade item.[/note]
allNodesLists.title: §2§lMore Compact Storage

allNodesLists.name: More Food, More Hearts
allNodesLists.data:
So, food is great, right? But what's even greater is eating tons of it! Too boring and pointless you say? Well, what if I told you you can get extra hearts just by expanding your palate. You get 1 point for every half shank of hunger from a food eaten, and after 50 points, you get 1 extra heart! Now you have a reason to make all those Pam's foods. Each food contributes its shank-value once. Eating something from a lunch box counts as if you took it out and ate it manually.

If you want to see what foods you've eaten, you can use the Food Journal, but it's clunky. Realistically, you want to use NEI to both see foods eaten and not eaten. You can search for 'not yet eaten' to see foods left, and 'assisted' to see foods eaten. You need to have started diminishing returns first to see this.

If it doesn't work, go to NEI options at bottom-left when the inventory is open, then click on Inventory, and change Search Mode to Regex. Then restart your client and try searching again.§r

There are also two commands:

/foodlist size
Tells you the overall progress, and the progress to the next heart.

/foodlist sync
Sync your food progression with the server if it gets out of sync.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lMore Food, More Hearts
allNodesLists.tooltip:
More Food, More Hearts

allNodesLists.name: Moron's Manual to Fecund Farms
allNodesLists.data:
If you ever wanted to know how crop breeding works, you are in the right place! Get some Crops - the sticks, that is - and some seeds from farming with a hoe or mattock. You can also place some plants and berries directly on crop sticks. Good plants to start with are flowers, wheat, cactus and sugarcane.

Make a plot of farmland with your tool and place water in the middle. For now, make 3x1 plots, separated by a row of dirt or cobble. You want to be able to see the center of each column of 3x1 plots all at once, like this:
FFFdddFFF
dddFFFddd
FFFdddFFF
dddFFFddd
FFFdWdFFF
dddFFFddd
FFFdddFFF
dddFFFddd
FFFdddFFF
Now place crop sticks in each end of the 3x1 plot. Then place the seeds on the sticks and wait a bit.

When they are almost fully grown you can put double crop sticks in the center spots by using crop sticks once more on already placed crop sticks. This center area can now grow new crops, even new species.

With some luck you might get a new unknown seed which can be scanned later.

Weeds need to be removed with a trowel or spade otherwise your field will become overgrown by them.

Using 3x1 plots is easy and not much work. Check them every 5-10 minutes to remove weeds and gather new seeds. If you forget, you only lose one or two seeds.

If you find a really nice seed, you can do 3x3 or 5x5 plots with the nice seed in the middle and others next to it for crossing. But this requires more babysitting since weeds could destroy the whole field.

Note that the more crops next to the double crop stick the faster new plants will show up, up to 4 obviously. This is also the way to get new versions of the same plant, you can't do it with just one parent like Agricraft.

Don't leave new crops in these intensive fields. Pull them out and hopefully get a seedbag. Put low stat seeds in production fields that don't require babysitting. Keep the high stat seeds for more crossing.

Crossing happens when two or more almost-mature crops are next to a double cropstick. There is a high chance of getting the same species as the parents. The rest of the time will be a mutation. For more details, check out the IC2 cropnalyzer quest.
allNodesLists.title: Moron's Manual to Fecund Farms
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Moron's Manual to Fecund Farms

allNodesLists.data: As you might know: tanned leather is more resistant and good enough for a backpack. Let's get a digger's backpack and a miner's backpack. Each pack holds different items. So use both for your first true back-packed mining experience.

allNodesLists.name: NEI is EVEN MORE POWERFUL NOW?
allNodesLists.data:
NEI now automatically collapses similiar items into one slot making browsing much faster! To collapse/uncollapse a group use ALT+LMB.
You can also create your own presets with custom groups!

[note]You can disable this functionality in NEI settings[/note]

Also now NEI has JEI-like Advanced Search:

@ - search by mod (@minecraft)

[note]There are even more special characters that you can use but most of them are off by default (e.g. no need to use # to search in tooltip), below are all the special characters, check which ones are on/off in NEI settings.

Space is used as a logical AND between different conditions
# - search by tooltip (#UV-Tier)
& - search by id: (&95:15 extratrees:door)
$ - search by ore dictionary ($ore)
% - search by subsets (%block)
| - logical or. multi-item search (wrench|hammer)
- - logical not. exclude items that match the following expression (-@minecraft)
" - multiple words wrapped in quotes are treated as one condition rather than several ("White Stained Glass")

Search Mode (apply on search parts, not full string):
Plain - simple string
Extended - allow only ?, * rules (by default)
Regex - allow full regex

In Extended Search Mode:
? - any character (@min?craft)
* - any few characters (@m*ft = @minecraft)
r/.../ - standard java regex (@r/m\w{6}ft/ = @minecraft)[/note]

[note]You can disable this functionality in NEI settingss.[/note]

You can add bookmarks with the A key while hovering over an item, also:
Hold SHIFT to bookmark the whole recipe
Hold CTRL to bookmark number of items
Hold SHIFT + CTRL to bookmark both recipe and all the number of all the items it contains
allNodesLists.title: §2§lNEI is EVEN MORE POWERFUL NOW?
allNodesLists.tooltip:
NEI is EVEN MORE POWERFUL NOW?
Prequest requests:
NEI is More Powerful Than You Imagine

allNodesLists.name: NEI is More Powerful Than You Imagine
allNodesLists.data:
NEI has some really nice advanced features too.

Clicking LMB or pressing R on an item shows the recipes to create it. RMB or U show recipes that use the item. Backspace moves you back to the previously browsed recipe.

Hold Shift to stop the oredict cycling through items, and to show the oredict entries for the current item under your cursor.

Search using @ to find all items from that mod; for example, §o@thaumcraft§r will list all Thaumcraft items and blocks.

You can combine multiple search terms with a space. §o@thaumcraft table§r will search for anything with table in the name or description, in the mod Thaumcraft.

It has even more advanced features than mentioned here and many configuration options, you can look in the NEI option menu under Inventory to find a few. Here you can change more things about how the search works (like using regex), toggle collapsible items or the item zoom panel, or configure the history panel to your liking.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lNEI is More Powerful Than You Imagine
allNodesLists.tooltip:
NEI is More Powerful Than You Imagine

allNodesLists.name: No Self-Healing Tools Here...Yet
allNodesLists.data:
New players might be surprised by finding the Tinker's Construct Ball of Moss in NEI not showing an actual recipe.

In this pack you have to first gain expertise in Thaumcraft to craft it. Go and become a dangerous wizard, and you'll gain the power needed to craft the Ball of Moss and make your tools heal themselves. Of course, you need to get to the Twilight Forest and get some aluminium ingots before you can begin. The Ball of Moss is in the GTNH tab of the Thaumonomicon, and requires infusion. There are many other great things in the Thaumonomicon, but be wary of warp.

Have a beer to prepare for your long journey.

allNodesLists.name: Not Enough Items - Now with Bookmarks and Recent History!
allNodesLists.data:
More like too many items! Here are some tips for using NEI.

When you have your inventory open, you can type the search terms in the text bar at the bottom. Make sure your GUI size is set correctly, or you won't be able to see it. Double-click the bar to highlight any matching items in your inventory or inventories you're looking at. Handy for searching for a specific ore, as they tend to look the same!

Even better, you can use T to search nearby inventories, which will emit some particles.

We have also provided the special Y command to look for a machine in the world, in case you've forgotten where you placed that Advanced Circuit Assembler.

We now have an extra-fancy Bookmark feature! The default key is A, but can be changed in the NEI config window. Bookmarks will be on the left side of the inventory, and you can look up their recipes or uses as normal. To move a bookmark, drag it with Shift+LMB. You can even bookmark entire recipes with Shift+A or recipes with amounts using Ctrl+Shift+A.

Pressing O will hide NEI, useful for fancy screenshots.

allNodesLists.name: Options For Finding Aluminium in This Tier
allNodesLists.data:
It can be hard to find Aluminum Gravel Ore on old servers or unlucky world seeds.

The alternatives are:
- Planting the Aluminum Ore Berries from the Smeltery quest,
- Searching for aluminium bars in chests,
- A recipe with XP buckets on a crafting table.

Once you reach LV, you can get aluminium from processing various ores or smelting Sapphire in an Electric Blast Furnace (EBF).
At MV, you can electrolyze clay dust or red granite dust. Check NEI for more options.

allNodesLists.name: Personally, I Prefer Pepsi™
allNodesLists.data:
You may have noticed that you can make more than just Charcoal in a Coke Oven, you can also make Coke.

The data below shows the burn time (BT), how long it takes in ticks - 20 ticks is 1 second - and how much creosote (Cr) you gain.

Coal 1600BT + 1800t -> Coal Coke 3200BT + 500l Cr
Wood Log 300BT + 1800t -> Charcoal 1600BT + 250l Cr
Cactus 50BT + 500t -> Cactus Charcoal 400BT + 30l Cr
Cactus Charcoal 400BT + 500t -> Cactus Coke 800BT + 30l Cr
Sugar Cane 50BT + 500t -> Sugar Charcoal 400BT + 30l Cr
Sugar Charcoal 400BT + 500t -> Sugar Coke 800BT +30l Cr

You want to save all of your Coke for making Steel in your Bricked Blast Furnace (BBF) later on. As for everything else, check NEI for the uses of each Coal variant, since there are many.

allNodesLists.name: Redstone, Early Game Processing
allNodesLists.data:
Are you wondering how to process raw redstone ore without a macerator?

Use the hammer in the crafting table to get some crushed redstone ore from your raw redstone ore. After that, use the hammer in the crafting table again to get some impure redstone dust.

Lastly, fill a cauldron with water and drop the whole stack of dust into it, either manually or by pressing Ctrl+Q. The cauldron can handle the entire stack with the same amount of water. You will get pure redstone dust for your redstone needs.

§3You could also take the hammer with you on your mining trip and break the redstone ore with it directly to get crushed redstone ore, thus skipping the raw redstone ore.
allNodesLists.title: §1§2§lRedstone, Early Game Processing

allNodesLists.name: Redstone? Haste!
allNodesLists.data: Mining and digging can be soooo slow. Get some redstone on your pick, shovel or axe to make it faster. You can use the Crafting Station to upgrade your tool 8 dust at a time. Later when you get a compressor you can use blocks to do 9 per block.

allNodesLists.name: The power of prospecting!
allNodesLists.data:
At the top of your map screen (J by default) there are multiple tabs, some of them will be very useful and will save you a ton of searching!

GT Oreveins - this tab will keep track of the veins for you, to save a vein to map right-click a naturally generated ore (some tools can't right click)
GT Underground fluids - this will help you later (MV)
TC Nodes - this tab will keep track of thaumcraft nodes for you (you need to scan them first)

[note]Small Ores are not part of veins and thus do not uncover a vein on the map. However veins generate extra small ores related to the vein in their chunks, so they can still be useful in your search (though not all small ores are related to a nearby vein so don't be fooled).[/note]

[note]Another great interaction is that you can use the NEI search bar in highlight mode (doubleclick it) and then go to the map screen to get the matching uncovered ore veins highlighted![/note]
allNodesLists.title: §6§lThe power of prospecting!
allNodesLists.tooltip:
The power of prospecting!
Prequest requests:
How the Heck Do I Find Ores?

allNodesLists.name: Tin
allNodesLists.data:
Tin ingots can be created by smelting Tin, Cassiterite, or Cassiterite Sand ore. Tin and Cassiterite ores are only found at high altitudes, but Cassiterite Sand ore is plentiful near the surface.

If you get lucky and find a high altitude Tin/Cassiterite vein, save one of the Cassiterite ore to find a Mica vein later on using the ore finder wand.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lTin

allNodesLists.name: Tinker-Time
allNodesLists.data:
While using your flint tools is fun in terms of killing pigs and cows, they are not long-lasting and can't be repaired. Plus Infernals laugh at your attempts to kill them. You discovered how to craft tools that can be repaired and upgraded, but for that you definitely need a more advanced crafting technique.

If you have to use wood other than oak to make your tables, you can convert them to the default oak wood type to complete this quest.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lTinker-Time

allNodesLists.name: Too Many Leaves
allNodesLists.data:
Want to clear out shrubbery but don't want to pull out leaves by hand? Need to find that last log hidden in the middle of a bunch of leaves?

Try an Iron Scythe! When used, it clears out a 5x5x5 area of leaves, crops, flowers, or grass. Excellent for tearing through Sacred Oak leaves or dense shrubbery in certain biomes. Later when you have a Cutting Machine you can upgrade to a Diamond Scythe with a 7x7x7 area of effect, or use Amethyst for 9x9x9 to FLEX.

The lower tiers break leaves instantly but don't seem to have the 3x3x3 range for some reason.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lToo Many Leaves

allNodesLists.name: Upgrade 2.0
allNodesLists.data:
Find iron, copper and tin ore. Very funny... How can you mine these with just a flint pickaxe?

I have an idea; bring me some of the stone you mined with your flint pickaxe and I will give you a better tool head in exchange.

Remember to level it up again either with monster heads or by mining.
allNodesLists.title: §2§k§l§l§r§2§lUpgrade 2.0
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Upgrade 2.0
Prequest requests:
Your First Tool
Copper Sky, Iron Curtain

allNodesLists.name: When All You Have is a Hammer...
allNodesLists.data:
...the whole world looks like a nail. When looking for good tool materials, see "GregTech Material Tools" tab in NEI. Remember that NEI bookmarks are your friends.

The GT tools each have special uses.

Screwdriver - Used on covers to change their behavior.

Wrench - Used to change the output direction on a GT machine, or to break it. Can also disconnect/connect pipes or enable their built in shutter.

Crowbar - Remove covers from machines or pipes.

Wire cutters - Connecting/disconnecting/breaking wires/cables.

Soft mallet - Turning machines on/off.

Hammer - Prospecting for ores in a limited way in front of you, and smashing ore blocks into crushed ores.

On a side note, Tin Pipes need a Steel Wrench to dismantle, so don't place them randomly.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lWhen All You Have is a Hammer...
allNodesLists.tooltip:
When All You Have is a Hammer...
Prequest requests:
Important Tools

allNodesLists.name: Wooden Door
allNodesLists.data:
For your new House you need some wooden doors. Well, the recipe is really hard and needs iron/copper and a lot of wood.

You can choose two more doors as a reward if you like.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lWooden Door

allNodesLists.name: XP Usage?!
allNodesLists.data:
Exploring some dungeons or fighting mobs probably gave you a lot of XP. Better use it to get iron, copper, tin, or other useful dusts before you die.

Place your tank on the ground and a drain on top. Now you can fill it with XP.

By the way, you discovered that while the seared tank doesn't hold much, it doesn't lose contents when broken, and full tanks can stack. I wonder if that information is useful...
allNodesLists.title: §2§lXP Usage?!
allNodesLists.tooltip:
XP Usage?!
Prequest requests:
Important Tools
You Are Now Prepared, Hopefully!

allNodesLists.name: You Need MOOOOOOORE Wood
allNodesLists.data:
It's time to feed your new coke oven with some wood to get more charcoal. You're looking for the most efficient way to plant trees. Try to find some spruce saplings and some jungle saplings. Both can be planted in a 2x2 grid to get bigger trees.

[warn]Warning label: Do not put your pets in the microwave to dry them. And do not plant any of these rewards in the middle of your base.[/warn]
allNodesLists.title: §2§lYou Need MOOOOOOORE Wood

allNodesLists.name: You Need Them All!
allNodesLists.data: There are many more backpacks: Hunter, builder, forester...
allNodesLists.title: §2§lYou Need Them All!
allNodesLists.tooltip:
You Need Them All!
Prequest requests:
Need More Space?

allNodesLists.name: Your First Bow
allNodesLists.data:
Since vanilla bows are only craftable in the assembling machine and mobs don't drop them very often you should make a Tinkers bow.

Wood would be the best material for now. Craft the bow limbs out of wood and the bow string out of strings. The arrow that has the most durability is bone, so craft the stick out of bone. It is much lighter but less durable than a regular arrow. Use a flint tip to make it repairable with flint.

You can repair your bow the same way as all the other Tinkers tools. The arrows can be regained by repairing them or picking them up from the floor. The arrows should be in your inventory if you want to pick up the ones you fired. You can't pick them up if they are in Battlegear slots.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lYour First Bow

allNodesLists.name: Your First Flint Throwing Knife
allNodesLists.data:
Is the bone bow too expensive for your taste? Then make a flint throwing knife instead. You need flint and a stick to get 12 knives. The durability and the attack damage are very low but it still helps with killing mobs from a safe distance.

The knives should be in your inventory if you want to pick up the ones you fired. You can't pick them up if the knives are in Battlegear slots.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lYour First Flint Throwing Knife

allNodesLists.name: Your First Tool
allNodesLists.data:
When your tinkers tables are ready, you can craft your first §oreal§r tool. If you didn't find a village yet to grab some parts from the chest, you can only craft flint tools.

Let's start with a pickaxe, an axe, and a shovel. At this point swords are unobtainable since they need metals like iron or bronze which you will get at a later stage. In the meantime use your gregtech swords.

Keep in mind that most of the original tool parts from Tinker's Construct are not shown in NEI. That doesn't mean that you can't craft them - use the tooltips on patterns and molds as guidance.

Your new tools are weak at first, but the more you use them the better they will get. You get a modifier slot after some levels, needing more as you level it up. They will level up to level 99 if you play long enough, with 20 modifier slots. Tool parts can be replaced for a bit of level XP, however the tool must be fully repaired first.

You need to level up the mining level each time you replace the parts to unleash the full power of the pickaxe. Stone->Copper for this pickaxe. If you manage to get a Zombie, Skeleton, or Creeper head, you can use it to skip the level-up process. This doesn't use up a modifier level, but does change the look until you change the pickaxe part out.

Item=Usable when mining level is X or less
Zombie=1
Skeleton=2
Creeper=4
Wither Skeleton=7
Nether Star=8

You could use a paper binding to add an extra modifier, but you will also get modifiers with tool levels.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lYour First Tool

allNodesLists.name: You Shall Proceed
allNodesLists.data:
As you've gathered and crafted all materials and tools you need for your basic steam machinery, you may now proceed to the next tier. Keep in mind that you'll need mountains of resources in order to craft even the simplest things, so you probably should stock up on all ores in this tier. But that's up to you.

As a special reward, you get a pair of Holo Glasses to look inside your inventories. Place it into the mask slot, and use the keybind to turn it on. Sometimes it gets turned off somehow, so try pressing the button if that happens.
allNodesLists.title: §2§lYou Shall Proceed
allNodesLists.tooltip:
You Shall Proceed

Making Bronze
Important Tools
When All You Have is a Hammer...

allNodesLists.name: A Better Way to Find Items
allNodesLists.data:
NEI has a built in search feature for finding an item stored in an inventory nearby. A Stockroom Catalog can give you a list of everything stored in your inventories.

Sneak right-click a block with an inventory (a chest, bookcase, barrel, anything with an inventory) to add that inventory to the list of inventories for the catalog to keep track of.

Sneak right-click the same block again to remove that block from the list.

A small particle effect will render on any block that has been selected with the catalog when holding the Stockroom Catalog to let you know that block is being tracked.

Right click to open the GUI and see the list. You can sort the list in ascending or descending order by quantity (Count) or alphabetical order.

You can also see a list of all the inventories that have a particular item and easily add the location of one of those inventories to a stockroom catalog so you can easily find your stuff.

The Stockroom Catalog can also be copied with the typesetting table and printing press.

Click on the title to change it to anything so you can custom label your stockroom catalog.

Click on the small chest icons on the right hand side of each listing to open the inventory list view.

If you want, you can craft a waypoint compass and use that to point you towards the chest. Since we have JourneyMaps and NEI, it's not really necessary.

[warn]The Catalog seems to be a bit broken though and doesn't work well with GT items.[/warn]
allNodesLists.title: §3§lA Better Way to Find Items
allNodesLists.tooltip:
A Better Way to Find Items
Prequest requests:
Books

allNodesLists.name: Accelerated Plant Growth
allNodesLists.data: As you might've discovered by now, plants grow very slowly. So why don't you try to speed that up a little? A watering can will come in handy.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lAccelerated Plant Growth

allNodesLists.name: A Clear View
allNodesLists.data:
Are you still living in your dirt/cobble hut? How about letting in some sunlight? Grind up some sand and flint and craft some glass dust. Put it in your smeltery and pour it into a casting basin to make clear glass.

[note]Hint: In order to use it for recipes, you have to chisel it.[/note]

[note]PS: The macerator no longer gives tiny piles, just uncraft a normal pile to get tiny ones. You'll appreciate this once you have a mixer in LV.[/note]
allNodesLists.title: §3§lA Clear View
allNodesLists.tooltip:
A Clear View
Prequest requests:
The Hell is That?

allNodesLists.name: Advanced Solar Boilers
allNodesLists.data:
Once you have some Steam machines, you can make Advanced Solar Boilers. They have more Steam output per second. Otherwise they are the same as Simple Solar Boilers.

Fill it with Water on the bottom side to produce Steam. Unlike the other Boilers, this only outputs Steam on the output port side.

Hint: The Advanced Solar Boiler calcifies and becomes less efficient over time - but it will only drop to 120L/s, not 40L/s, like the Simple Solar Boiler. Later on you can consider using Distilled Water to avoid calcification.

[note]You'll need Silver from the Twilight Forest (LV+) or from small ores for this.[/note]
allNodesLists.title: §3§lAdvanced Solar Boilers
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Advanced Solar Boilers
Prequest requests:
Better Than Iron
Time to Get Some Steel
The Power of the Sun

allNodesLists.name: A Fool Fit for a King
allNodesLists.data:
Only the craziest fool would use diamonds to make a tool! Or is it crazy like a fox?

§3PS: You can also §oburn them for fuel§r§3 for that extra bit of craziness.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lA Fool Fit for a King
allNodesLists.tooltip:
A Fool Fit for a King
Prequest requests:
Ooo, Shiny! (Not Platinum!)

allNodesLists.name: Alumite
allNodesLists.data:
It's upgrade time again. You could in principle make alumite by mixing obsidian, steel and aluminium in the smeltery. But to get a much better yield, you can show you are a GregTech hero and search NEI for an alternate recipe using dusts. Alumite pickaxes are able to mine ardite in the Nether.

Leave the rest of your Alumite as liquid in your smeltery, you'll want it to make the Tool Forge. You need 16 ingots in the smeltery to make 2 Large Plates.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lAlumite

allNodesLists.name: Another Use for Java, I Mean Lava
allNodesLists.data:
Now that you have Steel, you can craft a sturdy enough Boiler to handle Lava. Steam is only outputted in the back, and you require Water input on the side and Lava input on the top. But as an added benefit, this Boiler will reward you with Obsidian!

§3Did you know? Over 3 billion machines run on Lava!
allNodesLists.title: §3§lAnother Use for Java, I Mean Lava
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Another Use for Java, I Mean Lava
Prequest requests:
Where Can I Put All the Liquids?
Steam Alternatives
Time to Get Some Steel

allNodesLists.name: A Quite Different Storage
allNodesLists.data:
Regular chests can fill up rather quickly if you happen to collect mob drops like swords and/or armor. By using a cabinet, you can store up to 270 items of the same type. Also, it doesn't need a dolly - you can break it normally and it will retain contents.

Perfect for storing IC2 crop seeds, Forestry saplings, or bees!
allNodesLists.title: §3§lA Quite Different Storage

allNodesLists.name: A Very Important Alloy
allNodesLists.data:
The most important alloy (until you reach a higher tier) is undoubtedly red alloy. Fortunately, you have an alloy smelter, so grab some redstone and combine it with copper to get yourself a handful of that.

Don't confuse your bronze with your copper or else you'll be scratching your head.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lA Very Important Alloy
allNodesLists.tooltip:
A Very Important Alloy
Prequest requests:
More Advanced Alloys

allNodesLists.data: Are your cobblestone or dirt barrels filled to the brim? No problem, upgrade them!
allNodesLists.title: §3§lBarrel Upgrades
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Barrel Upgrades

Compressing Stuff

allNodesLists.data: Are your upgraded cobblestone or dirt barrels full again? No problem, upgrade them some more!
