allNodesLists.name: Basic Crafting: Machine Hulls
allNodesLists.data:
All machines need a hull to keep their private parts together. Good news is: They are crafted in the same way for every tier, only the materials change.

§3As noted on the tooltip, you can also use a machine hull to pass EU through, at 1A. This can be useful for a 1A diode on Thermos servers, splitting cables from 4A->1A or in a cleanroom later. You can also pass items or fluids through it.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lBasic Crafting: Machine Hulls
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Basic Crafting: Machine Hulls
Prequest requests:
Wired, Weird?!
Better Than Iron

allNodesLists.name: Basic Crafting: Motors
allNodesLists.data: Motors are little devices that can turn electrical power into rotational energy. Very useful for all kind of machines, and not that difficult to craft. The pattern is always the same, only the materials change with tiers. For now you can use redstone to magnetize your iron rod. Later on you will build an Electromagnetic Polarizer.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lBasic Crafting: Motors

allNodesLists.name: Basic Crafting: Rotors
allNodesLists.data: Rotors are also crafted using an identical pattern with different materials. A bit annoying to craft at the moment, but you don't need a lot of them anyway.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lBasic Crafting: Rotors
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Basic Crafting: Rotors
Prequest requests:
Basic Crafting: Machine Hulls

allNodesLists.name: Better Tank... Iron Tank
allNodesLists.data:
Storing more than 16 buckets of fluid in one tank? Sure! Just make an iron tank or upgrade the Buildcraft tank.

Diamond tanks carry up to 64 buckets and obsidian ones are blast proof. There's even more past that, but you should probably use GT tanks or large cells instead.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lBetter Tank... Iron Tank
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Better Tank... Iron Tank
Prequest requests:
Where Can I Put All the Liquids?

allNodesLists.name: Better Than Iron
allNodesLists.data:
But not as good as steel. Mostly, this is used in machine hulls, or in tools if you don't want to use steel up for that.

To make wrought iron, you need a tinkers smelter to melt some iron ingots down and cast nuggets; or use an ingot and a saw to get your nuggets. Now put these in a furnace to get wrought iron nuggets. With the compressor, you can compress the nuggets into ingots.

§3Hint: Crushed or purified iron ore (not a mixed version like pyrite, look for Iron Ore in Chalcopyrite veins) can be smelted to iron nuggets directly. Or you can use an alloy smelter to turn iron ingots into nuggets faster than a smeltery. You can also use a saw to cut up iron ingots into nuggets.

Later on, you can use an arc furnace to make wrought iron ingots directly.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lBetter Than Iron

allNodesLists.name: Blastoff!
allNodesLists.data: It's about time to make some steel. Look in the Multiblock Goals quest tab and build a Bricked Blast Furnace. Return here once you've made at least 8 steel ingots.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lBlastoff!

allNodesLists.name: Books
allNodesLists.data:
Books can be found easily enough in villages or in the roguelike dungeons surface brick house. I'm sure they have a recipe too.

Now glue on the other hand...or should I say horse? Try and get a horse inside a smeltery and feed it hay to keep it alive.

Or you can wait until after you go to the Nether and get some sulfur. Either way.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lBooks

allNodesLists.name: Bowl Full of Spaghetti
allNodesLists.data:
Or at least factories full of item pipes. With these simple item pipes and conveyors you can take items out of one machine and feed them immediately into a second machine.

Later on you can make better item pipes. Search for "item pipe" in NEI for options.

[warn]You'll need a Steel Wrench to remove them. Don't place them down unless you're sure of the location until you have one.[/warn]
allNodesLists.title: §3§lBowl Full of Spaghetti

allNodesLists.name: Circuit Boards
allNodesLists.data: For every circuit you need a circuit board. Craft a coated circuit board and use copper wire to finish it.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lCircuit Boards

allNodesLists.name: Compressing Stuff
allNodesLists.data: This rather simple device does a very important job: compression. It's main function is to press 9 ingots into a block, but it's also useful for a variety of recipes, for example making firm tofu.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lCompressing Stuff

allNodesLists.name: Cutting a Tree log by log is so Old School
allNodesLists.data:
By making a lumber axe, you are now able to cut down an entire tree in one hit. Don't forget your backpack when you're cutting a sacred oak down.

Protip: With wooden equivalents of casts, make an lumber axe completely out of netherrack - lower mining speed means less XP needed to level it up. Use the modifier slots to add Reinforced. Once you've leveled it up enough, upgrade the parts for better ones, such as steel, alumite, or others. The higher-level metals will require an MV Extruder. Keep in mind that the auto-smelt modifier doesn't work, so don't bother with it.

The quest will accept a lumber axe from any material.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lCutting a Tree log by log is so Old School
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Cutting a Tree log by log is so Old School
Prequest requests:
Tool Forge

allNodesLists.name: Extracting Stuff
allNodesLists.data: As you'll need rubber later to make cables from wires, you should get yourself a steam extractor. You can also use this machine to get more dyes from flowers, or process different fruits into juice.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lExtracting Stuff

allNodesLists.name: Extra Modifier
allNodesLists.data:
If you don't have an extra modifier on your tool you can easily add one. A gold block and a diamond are all you need.

You can add two more modifiers, but you'll need to read the tinkers book yourself to know what to use.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lExtra Modifier

allNodesLists.name: Factory Iron Door
allNodesLists.data:
For your new Factory you need iron doors. Unfortunately, the recipe is really hard, needing steel.

You can choose two more iron doors as reward if you like.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lFactory Iron Door

allNodesLists.name: Flaming idiots
allNodesLists.data:
Blazes are all infernals, and all nasty. Avoid like a plague. Get awesome weapons, awesome armor, and prepare for a fight.

The alternative is to figure out a way to destroy them with technology.

The alternative to the alternative is to figure out a different way to get blazepowder and blaze rods.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lFlaming idiots

allNodesLists.name: Flint and Steel
allNodesLists.data:
After you make steel you are able to craft flint and steel. I guess you'll want to travel to the Nether as soon as possible but be aware; the Nether is a very dangerous place.

Note: The ball of moss gives a tinker's tool self-repair. But if the tool is completely broken, it won't repair it.

Note that the flint and steel can take a few times to work.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lFlint and Steel

allNodesLists.name: GT6-Styled Wires and Cables
allNodesLists.data:
They work basically the same as pipes, but you need wire cutters (or a soldering iron) instead of a wrench. Additionally, you take damage if they're not insulated (wire) but not if they are (cable).

Hint: If you click one wire or cable on the other it will auto-connect. Cables and pipes can be painted to make sure you do not cross your MV line with your EV line, or dump hot lava into your plastic water pipes. No boom today.

Ha ha just kidding there is always a boom today!
allNodesLists.title: §3§lGT6-Styled Wires and Cables

allNodesLists.name: Gypsum
allNodesLists.data: To make bricks for the blast furnace you need concrete and gypsum. Gypsum can be found in a vein together with basaltic and granitic mineral sand, and fullers earth. Y 50-60 and only in the overworld.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lGypsum

allNodesLists.name: Hammer time v2
allNodesLists.data: Using 6 ingots to craft a hammer seems pretty wasteful, as this tool has durability. How nice would it be to have a machine that does the same but without having durability and using three ingots to make two plates? Guess what, there is one! And you should totally get one.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lHammer time v2
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Hammer time v2
Prequest requests:
One Anvil... Better Make That Two!

allNodesLists.name: Hoppers
allNodesLists.data: Hoppers come in handy when you want to automate your machines. You can input items via hoppers directly into GT pipes and you don't have to use a conveyor module. However, the input rate is much slower, and the hopper must be beneath its source inventory.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lHoppers

allNodesLists.name: How Can I Carry All These Items?
allNodesLists.data:
After you made your first steel, you are able to craft a small backpack. It has 36 slots, which is a bit more than a small chest. Later you can make it even larger.

You can have at most four of these backpacks in your inventory.

You can put one on your back and set it to automatically pick up stuff. In your controls, check that the command "Open Backpacks" has a key and doesn't have conflicts. The key only works after the backpack is added to the back slot, which can be done by using Shift+.
§r
You can rename your backpack by pressing Shift+RMB when holding it in your hand.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lHow Can I Carry All These Items?
allNodesLists.tooltip:
How Can I Carry All These Items?
Prequest requests:
Blastoff!

allNodesLists.name: How to Make Rubber
allNodesLists.data:
Making rubber is now more complicated - you need raw rubber and sulfur. Finding a sulfur vein in the Nether seems like a good idea, doesn't it? Found on Y 5-20. Later on you can get sulfur from chemicals like hydrogen sulfide or pyrite.

[warn]Sphalerite will be important later for gallium and zinc. Save it until you can fully process it in LV.[/warn]
allNodesLists.title: §3§lHow to Make Rubber
allNodesLists.tooltip:
How to Make Rubber
Prequest requests:
Extracting Stuff
THE NETHER

allNodesLists.name: How to open your Iron Doors?
allNodesLists.data:
Your iron doors make your Machine Hall or House more safe. They cannot be opened by hand.

Now let's craft some Pressure Plates and Buttons to open these heavy iron doors.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lHow to open your Iron Doors?
allNodesLists.tooltip:
How to open your Iron Doors?
Prequest requests:
Factory Iron Door

allNodesLists.name: I Ain't Afraid of no Ghost!
allNodesLists.data:
I've found a use for the Ectoplasm you can collect from spirits of the dead. It makes a very useful glass that you can walk on, but mobs cannot. However, they think they can!

So you can use this to create a moat around your base that drops mobs to the death in various ways, or just to shuttle them off somewhere else. Separate babies from mothers? Use it in a mob farm? Capture pigmen walking into the Overworld from your Nether portal? So many possibilities!
allNodesLists.title: §3§lI Ain't Afraid of no Ghost!
allNodesLists.tooltip:
I Ain't Afraid of no Ghost!
Prequest requests:
A Clear View

allNodesLists.name: I Know His Name!
allNodesLists.data:
The Name Remover is a simple utility machine that can strip off incorrect or useless NBT data. Only works on GT items?

§3Was more useful before NBT disassembly data was removed, but good riddance I (and basically everyone) say.

Lead is plentiful in the Twilight Forest. Or if you are desperate, small ores can be found in the Nether.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lI Know His Name!
allNodesLists.tooltip:
I Know His Name!
Prequest requests:
Better Than Iron
Rubber Sheets

allNodesLists.name: It's a Dirty Job, and You're Going to Do It
allNodesLists.data: The Plunger is used to clear liquids from pipes. It can also be used on a machine to remove up to 1000mb of fluid from its internal buffer. So you don't have to wrench your machine and re-place it. It can be crafted from a rod of the desired material and rubber sheets.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lIt's a Dirty Job, and You're Going to Do It
allNodesLists.tooltip:
It's a Dirty Job, and You're Going to Do It
Prequest requests:
Rubber Sheets

allNodesLists.name: Jacques Cousteau
allNodesLists.data:
Now that you have a Scuba Helmet you can safely explore underwater for long periods of time. You just need some compressed air cells. I'll trade you some Tin ingots for a few compressed air cells.

As your air drops, the helmet will take a compressed air cell and give back an empty cell. Throw these cells into your compressor and you can easily gather clay from beneath rivers. You'll be able to make more cells later once you get an extruder or a plate bender.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lJacques Cousteau

allNodesLists.name: Key to Your Heart
allNodesLists.data: Barrels by default allow locking the barrel to a specific item, even when empty. For drawers however you will need to make the Drawer Key to lock its content types.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lKey to Your Heart

allNodesLists.name: Lapis, Lazurite, Sodalite, Calcite
allNodesLists.data:
In order to make your bricked blast furnace you need to find a lapis vein containing calcite.

You can find the vein in the overworld at Y 20-50.

allNodesLists.name: Lapis? Lucky!
allNodesLists.data:
Maybe you were lucky and received the luck modifier on your pickaxe. If not, you may still have an unused modifier on your pick so you can add some lapis lazuli. Or you can perhaps add another modifier by adding a diamond and a gold block to your pick and then add some lapis.

You can put the lapis lazuli in more than one slot in the tool station, use blocks to raise the luck level faster, and even use lapis blocks in the crafting station with your tool for maximum luck gain.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lLapis? Lucky!

You have found an alternative way of making charcoal with a "charcoal pile igniter".

Go and start getting massive amounts of charcoal.

If this is your first multiblock, look at the extended tooltip (hold shift) or visit [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Charcoal_Pile_Igniter[/url] to see how to make it work.

allNodesLists.name: Lucifer's Little Helper
allNodesLists.data:
With an alloy smelter and some netherrack dust you can make Nether furnaces, which are extremely efficient cooking machines. Very handy for someone needing a lot stuff furnaced in a jiffy.

The only downside is that iron furnaces can be used in the EBF later on. Nether furnaces cannot. Then again, Nether dust is practically free, so what's the loss? You can always use them to bake stacks of bread!

allNodesLists.data:
Finally you are able to make a device that will replace your mortar. However, the "no-durability" feature of this device comes with a cost: You need 2 diamonds for the grinding heads.

The macerator will double your ore output. Put ores through it instead of smelting directly.

§3NOTE: Remember, don't block the output port and don't stand behind it.§r

allNodesLists.data:
After you can make steel and have a tinkers smelter you can make molds. Molds can be used in the alloy smelter and the fluid solidifier. You need them to make vacuum tubes, ingots, gears and more.

[note]PS: The 'shapes' are for the Extruder.[/note]

allNodesLists.name: More Advanced Alloys
allNodesLists.data:
Your smeltery does a great job mixing metals into alloys, but it's not very efficient, and limited in its complexity. You need something new, so why not put your steam to some use? The Alloy Smelter can make bronze for you directly, using ingots, dusts, or even nuggets. You can make a nugget mold as well to turn ingots into nuggets if you have steel.

It might also come in handy when processing raw rubber. You should keep an eye on recipes to see when machines offer better options to make items...

[note]NOTE: Like all steam machines, the output port is a steam outlet when recipes complete. It must not be blocked. Also, steam is hot, remember? Change the output side by whacking the machine with a wrench. The 3x3 grid will show you which side the output will move to when you whack it.[/note]

You can empty the machine by putting a hopper beneath it.

[warn]WARNING: The Alloy Smelter recipes take a lot of steam.[/warn] Do them one by one until you understand how fast you use steam, and how much you will need buffered. Large pipes are a decent "poor man's" buffer, and the boiler can hold quite a bit of steam, as well as the machine itself. Once you get a little further along, make a larger steam buffer with an iron or steel railcraft tank.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lMore Advanced Alloys
allNodesLists.tooltip:
More Advanced Alloys

allNodesLists.name: Moving Your Tanks, Chests, and Barrels
allNodesLists.data:
Want to move your chests and barrels without spilling all the things (buildcraft™)? No problem! Make a dolly and you can carry your full chests, barrels or storage drawers anywhere you want. But be warned, you will get a slowness debuff so hopefully you don't have to travel very far. You can also move non-portable buildcraft and iron tanks without losing fluids, and worktables without losing stored recipes.

Shift right click an empty dolly to collapse it. It won't carry anything until you unfold it, but it will stack and can go in your backpack.

§3PS: Later on you can fly or make a traveller's belt to get around the debuff.§r

allNodesLists.name: Multiblock Revolution
allNodesLists.data:
The steam machines you have been using until now have served you well, but there will be a time when you need to process even more items. That's where the so-called multiblocks come in. There’s a variety of steam multiblocks available to you - go have a look at the Mass Processing quest tab!

This tab introduces you to a wide range of extremely powerful multiblock machines that can replace your old, worn-out singleblocks (and some that can replace your old multiblocks!). Many of these new machines will require you to handle additional mechanics and requirements, but it will be worth it!

Here are some terms you should be familiar with as you enter the world of multiblocks:

Overclock (OC):
If a machine can handle at least 4 times the voltage that is required for a recipe, it will overclock - causing it to require 4x the EU/t but also run 2x as fast. This can happen multiple times!

Perfect Overclock (Often phrased as "Does not lose efficiency when overclocked):
Some machines conditionally (or unconditionally) perform perfect overclocks: in this case, the machine will require 4x the EU/t, but it will run 4x as fast instead, leading to both increased speed and no net increase in the total eu usage!

Parallel (Often phrased as "Processes x items"):
Machines which parallel act as if they are running multiple of themselves - that is to say, they are able to perform multiple of the same recipe at the same time, using the recipe's EU/t multiplied by the number of parallels. Machines which parallel will [warn]PRIORITIZE[/warn] this behavior over overclocking, which is good for you! Parallels are more efficient.

[note]When working with multiblocks, if power is interrupted during operation, your inputs will be lost forever... careful![/note]
allNodesLists.title: §3§lMultiblock Revolution

§3PS: In many cases this is not worth it, since the tools don't degrade that fast, it doesn't cost much to repair, and you get better materials (with higher durability) to make them out of reasonably fast. However, there are a few very nice use cases like lumber axes and tools for automation setups.

Let's make a mold for the rubber sheets. They are mainly used for conveyors and cables.

At this stage, making cables by hand with rubber sheets is faster and cheaper in power than the Alloy Smelter recipe for the cables.

allNodesLists.name: Safety First
allNodesLists.data:
For those new to GregTech, here are some tips and warnings about electricity.

Machines don't like being out in the rain, and will start fires nearby. Fires next to a machine have a random chance of an explosion. Also, sending a higher voltage than a machine's tier causes an explosion. Or several, if you pack things together, like many people. Sending more amps than a machine can use doesn't harm anything though.

Sending too high a voltage or too many amps down a cable will cause the cable to burn up and start fires, which may then cause machine explosions. Make sure the number of amps provided by generators and buffers to a cable does not exceed the amps it is capable of carrying.

A generator that supplies 1A can possibly feed multiple machines, if their recipes require less than the full voltage. For example, macerators processing ore only need 2 EU/t, so you could run several from a single 1A generator, as long as the wires aren't too long. Why does that matter? Because there's loss for every amp for every block, listed on the wire/cable. Note that cables are better than wires. But be careful! Sometimes a recipe needs a lot more EU than you expect, like a macerator sand -> quartz dust recipe.

Most machines only use 1A, however there are exceptions, such as the arc furnace, thermal centrifuge, world accelerators, and the UUM machines. Note that machines can accept more amps than they use (usually 2) in order to top up their energy supply, especially if they didn't recieve most of the amp because of loss (mostly a problem in LV). The formula is (EU/t of Recipe * 2) / Voltage Tier + 1. Keep this in mind when deciding on cables.

Some machines are specifically there to help you deal with multiple amps, such as battery buffers, transformers, and diodes. Check out the quest tab Storing and Transforming EU for more on those.

If you want to send more amps, use a larger cable or a superconductor (MV+, but ULV and LV have their own lossless cables). You can use laser hatches much later to send even more. There even are wireless options, but not right now.

A single block machine starved of EU will restart progress but not lose the recipe items. A multiblock machine will lose the items.

Note that any block that emits EU has loss when doing so: 2 ^ (tier-1) per amp. So 1 EU at LV, 2 EU at MV, and so on. Using large numbers of battery buffers in a row is thus very wasteful of your power. You have to be careful with losses when making your first EBF later in LV, maybe rather power them directly? Of course, if you want to keep your amps topped up over longer distances, you'll need to place BBs occasionally to 'top up' the amps, though this is less the case the further ingame you get, as the loss becomes less of something to worry about.

If this info isn't enough for you, head on over to [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Electricity[/url] to read more.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lSafety First

allNodesLists.name: Slime Island Journey
allNodesLists.data:
Rubber trees are not the only source for raw rubber. Go and find a slime island high in the sky. Slime balls and slime leaves give raw rubber too.
Make some slime tree farms beside your rubber farm.

§3Liquid slime is not allowed to be placed down, as it acts as a spawner, and can cause lag.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lSlime Island Journey

allNodesLists.name: Steam-a-licious!
allNodesLists.data:
You've almost made it. One last crafting step is required in order to advance to Tier 1. Keep going!

This Steam Turbine generates electricity from Steam. The power source you've been using is the same, but from this point on you will generate EU, and bring it to your machines via cables, instead of bringing the Steam directly to them. Luckily, electric machines don't need an exhaust port, and they are considerably more efficient than Bronze machines.

At a later point, you will most likely switch from Steam to another fuel, though.

allNodesLists.name: Tame an Ocelot to Get a Friend
allNodesLists.data:
Once you have the required materials, you will need to find an ocelot to tame.

Ocelots can be found in Jungle Biomes.

If you are having trouble finding an ocelot, you can always summon an ocelot using a spawn egg.

You can tame an ocelot by giving it a raw fish. So add the raw fish to your inventory and select the raw fish in your hotbar.

Just like vanilla Minecraft, a tamed ocelot turns into a cat. The cat will repel creepers.

§3TIP: Make sure you are in a large space when trying to tame the ocelot so that the ocelot has lots of room to move. If you are in a space that is too small, you will not be able to tame the ocelot.

Next, while holding the raw fish, do not move. If you move, you will scare away the ocelot. If you are very still, the ocelot will eventually notice the fish in your hand and begin to walk over to you.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lTame an Ocelot to Get a Friend

Tame an Ocelot to Get a Friend

allNodesLists.name: The GT Tank, ULV Version
allNodesLists.data:
This is the first GT-type tank. It stores 32 buckets or 32,000L, and can be used to I/O cells. The ULV Tank from GT++ needs steel plates, iron plates, tin plates, a clay pipe, and a water bucket.

GT tanks do not auto-output. If you want to move fluids out of the tank, use a GT pump, conduit, or something similar.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lThe GT Tank, ULV Version

§3PS: Infernals can drop them, though you won't get credit for the quest that way.

allNodesLists.name: The Iron Guy
allNodesLists.data:
Do you feel lonely? Need some extra protection in your base? Want to keep the pigmen off your back in the Nether? Craft some Iron Golems and the monster problem inside your base will be gone.

They can do good amounts of damage and aggro enemies like the pigmen away from you. They can even take care of that pesky Vampire Pigman.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lThe Iron Guy

allNodesLists.name: THE NETHER
allNodesLists.data:
Now more dangerous with extra hardcore infernal mobs. Have fun and take care. Remember that the flint and steel can take a few times to work, but there are other ways to make fire ...

Be sure to bring a tough companion along to keep you alive. If you have no friends, why not make an Iron Golem and push it through first, or bring the materials for more along with you?

Also, §lwhen§r you die here, not if, your graves will spawn skeletons because of the darkness. Make sure you light up areas where you might die, and when recovering graves light up the area §lfirst§r so that you don't end up dying over and over and making a mess.

Watch out for some mobs! They'll take minimal damage from any weapon that is not their weakness. So if you seem to not be doing much damage, you probably aren't! Think about other options to hurt/kill the monster.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lTHE NETHER

allNodesLists.name: The one book to rule them all
allNodesLists.data:
This Tome can store multiple documentation books from other mods. It will be empty when crafted, but you can add books by combining it with the desired book in a crafting grid.

Right-clicking with the Tome in hand will open an interface showing all the added books; clicking on a book will transform the tome into the selected book. To revert it back to the Tome, left-click while sneaking.

To retrieve a stored book, transform the Tome into the desired book and throw it away while sneaking - this will drop the selected book and leave the tome in your inventory.

[warn]Some warnings:

The extended version of the Book of Biomes from Witchery is not compatible with this tome.

You should not throw it through the Botania portal. The elves might steal your Tome and return only their own copy of the Lexica Botania.[/warn]
allNodesLists.title: §3§lThe one book to rule them all

allNodesLists.name: The Power of the Sun
allNodesLists.data:
The sun has quite a bit of power, so why not use it to produce Steam?

Fill it with Water on the bottom side to produce Steam. Unlike the other Boilers, this only outputs Steam on the output port side.

You need Silver from small ores to craft Solar Boilers. Later in LV you can get much more in the Twilight Forest.

§3Hint: The Simple Solar Boiler calcifies and becomes less efficient over time, dropping down to a minimum of 40L/s. Later on you can consider using Distilled Water to avoid calcification.

allNodesLists.name: Welcome to Tier 0.5, Steam!
allNodesLists.data:
Welcome, and well done so far! This tier is all about your first machines, getting more stuff from your ores and making bronze ingots in a more efficient manner.

For water, check out the Water Siding Tank multiblock in the Multiblock goals tab.

To connect up your boilers, be sure to provide water from the bottom, they'll accept only water from this side, so no risk of melting your pipe. Wooden pipes are fine for this. Make sure you never run out of water - [warn]adding water to a dry hot boiler will cause it to explode![/warn]

Steam will come out from the sides. Remember, steam is hot! It will destroy wooden pipes. And it can burn you if you walk on bronze pipes full of steam. Cover them with wooden planks or paper. Or just don't walk on/next to them.

And no, you can't automate it. Make an electric one if you want to do that.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lWelcome to Tier 0.5, Steam!
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Welcome to Tier 0.5, Steam!

You Shall Proceed

allNodesLists.name: What Engineer Doesn't Want a Portable Workbench?
allNodesLists.data:
This backpack sacrifices some space to give you a portable crafting table. You have to put the items you want to craft inside the backpack. Because of this, you can use it to quickly craft large amounts of items at once.

You can also use the Forestry Worktable with its larger inventory to do the same. Once you reach MV, you can switch to an Adventure Backpack that includes a pair of tanks for storing fluids if you want.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lWhat Engineer Doesn't Want a Portable Workbench?
allNodesLists.tooltip:
What Engineer Doesn't Want a Portable Workbench?

How Can I Carry All These Items?

allNodesLists.name: Where Can I Put All the Liquids?
allNodesLists.data:
With your brand new alloy smelter you are able to combine two materials. What happens if you mix some obsidian dust and thickened glass? Obsidian glass, great. Your first tank that you can make would be a Buildcraft tank. This tank can carry up 16 buckets of a single fluid. It's possible to upgrade those tanks so they can hold up to 64 buckets.
You can also stack the tanks to increase capacity.

Where Can I Put All the Liquids?

A Clear View

allNodesLists.name: Wired, Weird?!
allNodesLists.data: Two of the very basic materials for machines are wires and cables. For cables you can either use a rubber sheet in the crafting table or use rubber bars in the alloy smelter. Not very efficient, but there will be a better way later.

allNodesLists.data: Small gears require a wire cutter to be made, so let's craft one.

allNodesLists.name: Wire-Wrap
allNodesLists.data: Placing wires without insulation seems to be a bad idea. Now that you have an extractor to extract raw rubber out of sticky resin and an alloy smelter to further process it using sulfur, you should work on getting some insulating rubber bars.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lWire-Wrap

allNodesLists.name: Wooden Bolts
allNodesLists.data:
Your crossbow need some ammo to shoot with. Let's craft some wooden bolts. For now, you can put either iron, alumite, or steel on the tip of your bolts using the Smeltery. For higher tier bolts and tips you will need to pump metals into a Fluid Solidifier with the correct tool rod inserted.

[warn]For upgrades:[/warn]
[note]Nether Quartz - More damage
Moss - Self-Repair (unlock in GTNH Thaumcraft tab)[/note]
allNodesLists.title: §3§lWooden Bolts

allNodesLists.name: Wooden Crossbow
allNodesLists.data:
Now you are able to make a better long range weapon - a crossbow. Use wood for the the crossbow limb and the body and use obsidian (Reinforced III) for the tough binding. Normal strings for the bowstrings would be enough for now.

Assemble the bow yourself on your tool forge.

[warn]For upgrades:[/warn]
[note]Redstone - Speed on the draw
Lapis - Fortune on kills
Moss - Self-repair (this is not visible in NEI until you unlock it in the GTNH Thaumcraft tab)[/note]

§6NOTE: Some mobs require damage from specific tools. IF YOU ARE SHOOTING AT SOMETHING AND IT IS NOT GETTING HURT, *RUN*. And then figure out what weapon might be best to kill it.
allNodesLists.title: §3§lWooden Crossbow

allNodesLists.name: Working Table 2.0
allNodesLists.data:
A manual crafting table which remembers the last nine used recipes. Left click one of the recipes shown in the right-hand side to automatically fill in the crafting grid. Right-click to lock a memorized recipe and prevent a newer recipe from bumping it off.

Resources need to go into the internal inventory. The crafting matrix is only a visual representation.

The Forestry worktable is super-useful, and can reduce the tedium of many common jobs because you can click-drag across a row of items, and it will use tools in its own inventory to continue crafting.

Specifically:
Making with - Put all the ingredients into the table, and if the recipe is selected, shift click the result to craft them all at once (until you run out)
Making fresh water for Pam's - Same as above, but no second item
Making clay bricks - The wooden form is automatically reused
Making anything that uses a tool - Also automatically reused, while consuming durability

[warn]Warning: Stored recipes will be lost if the worktable is broken! To avoid this, move it using a dolly.[/warn]

[note]For more forestry quests you need to go to the dedicated tab.[/note]
allNodesLists.title: Working Table 2.0

allNodesLists.data: Steam machines are quite stupid, they just do one thing over and over again. As you advance into the electrical age, you've decided that you want the machines to have more features, like automatic output in order to create some automation. For that, you need electronic circuits.

allNodesLists.name: Analyzing the Soil
allNodesLists.data:
Tired of looking for ores by hand? Want to find underground oil that will last a long time? A seismic prospector will tell you the ores in the surrounding chunks in a (sorta) handy book you can read, and also the underground fluids beneath you. It doesn't need to be powered.

To determine which kind of fluid there is in the chunk you need to scan the soil by right clicking an Advanced Seismic Prospector with 2 Powderbarrels, 4 Glyceryl Trinitate cells, 8 iTNT or 16 TNT. This one doesn't explode the user too on use. Features! There are four types of oil or natural gas for the overworld. See the quest in Tips and Tricks once you've made an oil drill.

1) Right click explosives.
2) Use a single Data Stick to extract the data by right clicking on it after the animation has finished. Each will hold ONE result.
3) Next you need to put the data stick in a GT scanner to have it analyzed.
4) Place the analyzed data stick in the bottom right slot of a printer and add 3 paper in the top left slot and make sure you have at least 144L squid ink in it.
5) Take the printed pages and combine it with a piece of leather in an assembling machine filled with at least 20 mb of refined glue.

[note]TADA![/note] Now you have a book with detailed info about the chunks you scanned. Visual Prospecting adds the information to your map the moment you make the book.

§2Data Sticks are not easy (or possible) to make right now, so do not lose them.§r You can put it in a crafting table to erase it when done.

Ore locations are given as the center of the chunk. Ores that are marginal in that chunk may not be found in the center but on an edge. Look at where ores are located and determine the center of the vein. At higher tiers, it scans more chunks for ores. If you just want to know about fluids, use the lower tier version so the book isn't as long.

Each underground fluid field is 8x8 chunks. This starts at 0,0 and continues for 8 chunks east and south, containing 64 chunks. Not all fields have anything in them though. Within the field the amount can vary +/- 25 percent. The amount reported in the book is the minimum and maximum per field across all chunks in the field. The prospector reports on 3x3 fields (as in, 9 fields of 8x8 chunks) at all tiers with the center field where the seismic prospector is located. Fluid extraction rate depends on many factors, check the wiki for details. In general, anything above 300 is really good. The total amount in the chunk is complicated.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lAnalyzing the Soil
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Analyzing the Soil

Scanning Bees, Crops and Moooooore!

allNodesLists.name: A New Alloy - Cobalt Brass
allNodesLists.data:
If you want to cut diamond blocks into plates, it's time to get a new alloy, Cobalt Brass.

First you need to make brass out of zinc (only found in small ores in the Overworld, in Nether Sphalerite, or as a centrifuge byproduct from tin or tetrahedrite) and copper. Mix it with aluminium and cobalt dust (you can get it as a byproduct of a couple ores, go searching in the nether, or go to the Twilight Forest for Cobaltite) to get the cobalt brass dust.

Now that you've come this far, we think that you're able to look up the ores that you need by yourself with the help of NEI.

allNodesLists.tooltip:
A New Alloy - Cobalt Brass

allNodesLists.name: A New Alloy - Magnalium
allNodesLists.data:
Wondering why you need magnalium now? It's not for GT machines but for a material update for your crossbow.

You already made some Aluminium dust before. Getting Aluminium will become easier once you get an EBF or MV electrolyzer.

Combine Aluminium and Magnesium in your alloy smelter to get Magnalium.

A New Alloy - Magnalium

allNodesLists.name: Antimony
allNodesLists.data: The most efficient way to get antimony for batteries is to run stibnite through a BBF or EBF, burning off the impurities (sulfur), and giving you more antimony. You can also centrifuge it if you want to keep the sulfur. You can also centrifuge tetrahedrite dust if you're desperate.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lAntimony

allNodesLists.name: Ardite and Cobalt
allNodesLists.data:
If you have some time you can look for cobalt and ardite in the Nether.

You've heard rumors of a special wood only found in another land, a forest of Twilight, that can make tools strong enough to mine them.

Remember, you need an electric blast furnace to process these materials before you can make tools with them.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lArdite and Cobalt

allNodesLists.name: Ardite Crossbow Body
allNodesLists.data:
To make your crossbow even better, craft an ardite crossbow body. You received a few ardite ingots as reward before but will need to find ore in the Nether and process it in an Electric Blast Furnace.

With redstone you can make your bow faster. This requires a free modifier slot on your crossbow.

Don't bother putting Nether Quartz on the crossbow, it only improves damage from whacking mobs over the head with it. Put the Nether Quartz on your bolts instead.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lArdite Crossbow Body

allNodesLists.name: A Truly Sharp Saw Blade
allNodesLists.data: Combining cobalt brass and diamond dust makes a really sharp saw blade for your cutting machine.

A Truly Sharp Saw Blade

allNodesLists.data: The Auto Workbench is a simple automated crafting system. You place ghost items in the grid to create the recipe, and place components in the inventory. They will slowly be converted into the crafted item. While not fast and can only do 1 recipe each, it does support automation - only items acceptable to the recipe are allowed in the inventory. It does not use power.

Automated Crafting​

allNodesLists.data: Your hoe must be getting worn out by now. Why not craft an electric one which never breaks?
allNodesLists.title: §6§l§d§5§lAutomated Farmer

allNodesLists.name: Automated Sticky Resin Farmer
allNodesLists.data:
If you're tired of crafting tons of tree taps, how about a machine that uses power but never breaks? Let's craft an electric tree tap!

(If you're looking for better ways to get Sticky Resin, you might want to consider the Stickreed crop from IC2 crops. To get it, plant Sugarcanes on Crops on a X formation, with spaces between them, and then put 2 Crops on each empty slot. For more information, check the crop quests.
allNodesLists.title: §5§6§l§5§lAutomated Sticky Resin Farmer

allNodesLists.name: Auto Mining
allNodesLists.data:
Automatic mining in LV tier? Wow! This nifty machine will collect ores for you, which can be helpful especially in the Nether, as it won't anger pigmen.

Place up to two stacks of mining pipes in the right slots. Each pipe can go 1 block, and allow the miner to dig 1 block further. If you're above Y64, you may need to pipe more in.

This machine only needs 8 EU/t to work, so LV batteries in a batbuff work ok if you don't want to make another generator.

The miner searches for ores in a 17x17 block work area (adjustable with a screwdriver), and comes with a level 1 fortune bonus! Great for gathering additional small ores!

Don't forget to cover it up! These are GT machines, so remember to protect them (and their power sources!) from rain on all sides. And set a waypoint with JourneyMap so you don't forget where you placed it if you place it far away! You'll need to chunkload the miner if you want it to keep working when you're not there.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lAuto Mining

allNodesLists.name: Avengers, Assemble!
allNodesLists.data:
An absolute must have for fans of the movie. Oh, and to make all the things, of course. There's a number of recipes that take less materials to make in the assembler, or can only be made with it, so make it ASAP!

You can use the battery slot and the other extra slot in the GUI to store unused configuration circuits.

If you've completed the Silverwood quest on the first tab, you can go to the Twilight Forest after making your Assembler. See the Novice Thaumaturgy tab for details.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lAvengers, Assemble!

allNodesLists.name: Basic Arc Furnace
allNodesLists.data:
The arc furnace is an alternative to macerating stuff back into dusts and for making wrought iron, annealed copper, and glass (in MV). You get ingots, and sometimes different materials back from recycling than with a macerator. You also have all 4 slots at LV. The recipes use oxygen and 3A of power.

Just ignore the plasma one.

And no, you can't just send 1A of MV. That will blow it up.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lBasic Arc Furnace

allNodesLists.name: Basic Canner
allNodesLists.data:
The canning machine is used to fill batteries, fill cells with stuff (usually dust, not used that often), or to fill tin cans with any kind of food (HV+).

At LV-HV tier you can make batteries with sodium, cadmium, or lithium.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lBasic Canner

allNodesLists.name: Basic Circuit Assembler
allNodesLists.data:
Advanced (HV) circuits require an LV circuit assembling machine. Basic (LV) and Good (MV) ones can also be made much more efficiently with this machine.

However, all circuit assemblers need higher tier circuits than the other machines of their tier. This means you have to use MV circuits instead of the LV ones you've been using until now. I know you want it, so make it already!

Basic Circuit Assembler

allNodesLists.data:
To get your molten fluids back to a solid state you need a fluid solidifier. This is handy for processing molten rubber directly from the chemical reactor. It's used for crossbow bolts as well.

Keep in mind that GT fluids are different from Tinker's Construct. You will mainly work with GT fluids going forward.

allNodesLists.data: Monsters spawning in or near your base can be annoying. Especially if you happen to get infernal creepers. Luckily, there's a good way to prevent them from spawning at all.

Macerating ores usually doubles the output. If you want MOOOOOOORE, craft an ore washer and wash out some rare materials.

Note that these both use water, and are painfully slow.

Put crushed ore in them.

[note]You can also consider using the steam multiblock instead if you want.[/note]

allNodesLists.name: Battery Alloy
allNodesLists.data:
Mixing antimony and lead in the alloy smelter will give you battery alloy. Combine it with tin cable and voila, there's your small battery hull.

Small = LV, Medium = MV, Large = HV. It gets weirder after that.

Note that if you make the battery alloy in the mixer you need to use dusts, but if you use the alloy smelter you can use either.

Check out the quest tab Storing and Transforming EU for all details about EU power storage.

This thing can be laggy, so be careful about letting too many xp orbs out of the tank. Apply a RS signal to turn it off.

allNodesLists.name: Better Gallium and Arsenic Sources
allNodesLists.data:
There are a couple of ways to increase your Gallium.

1. Breed Zinc Bees and react the Gallium Combs with Hydrochloric Acid. The bee is not too deep in the breeding progression and the processing only requires LV.

2. Use IC2 crops under the Farming tab to get Galvania leaves, to 4x your zinc and sphalerite crushed ores to purified ores.

3. Use the HV macerator on the centrifuged ores to get a 10 percent chance of a whole Gallium dust.

4. Use plentiful Bauxite ores from the Moon.

5. Kill Redcaps/Redcap Sappers in Twilight Forest. Also Kobolds drop Arsenic.

6. Duplicate nugget with Thaumcraft. This requires §lTaboo§r researches, so you might not want to do this.

For Arsenic, Cobaltite ore in the Twilight Forest is a great source for more information go to the quest "Cobalt and Arsenic from Cobaltite".

Cobaltite can also be multiplied 4x by the IC2 crop Nickelback.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lBetter Gallium and Arsenic Sources
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Better Gallium and Arsenic Sources

Gallium Arsenide Crystal

allNodesLists.name: Biomes Everywhere, But Not the One You Want?
allNodesLists.data:
Tired of searching all over the map for that Bamboo Forest or Tropical Rainforest? Desperate for clay dust and need to find a Canyon or Mesa biome? Nature's compass will lead you to the biome you're looking for, if it's within its range.

The compass menu has the following functionality:
* When Sorted By: Name, you can filter the list by name or its parts. The search is case-insensitive.
* You can search by keys and their combinations. For instance, name: bamboo, climate: warm, bh: -1.8, tag: forest.
All available keys are:
name,
climate [hellish, hot, warm, normal, cold, icy],
baseheight | bh (float, can be negative),
heightvariation | hv (float),
rainfall | rain (float),
temperature | temp (float),
humidity [damp, normal, arid],
tags.

Some things to keep in mind:
* Biomes from other dimensions show up on the list, don't bother searching for those unless you're in that dimension.
* In general, the full list has biomes that are not generated by Realistic World Generator, like Sunflower Plains.
* Radius 10000 means it couldn't find the biome. In this case after the initial search, its menu will show only the biomes in the 10k radius. Use Shift+RMB to see the whole list again.
* You can try again at a different location - the range is 10k from your current position.
* Artificially created biomes count, so remove them if you want to find a natural one.
* There's lots of different 'versions' of biomes under the same category, so if you want a tropical one for tropical bees, there's actually a bunch of places you can get it.
* For those who don't mind the freeze when searching, the radius can be changed in a config. The HUD position can also be changed in the config.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lBiomes Everywhere, But Not the One You Want?
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Biomes Everywhere, But Not the One You Want?

Avengers, Assemble!

allNodesLists.name: Black and Decker
allNodesLists.data:
Tired of having to replace tools all the time because they constantly break? Now that Steel is available, it's time to make some electric versions of the Screwdriver and Wrench! Charge them up like Batteries, and they'll last much longer than the non-electric versions of these tools.

You can use Lithium Batteries, or if you're on a budget, Cadmium or Sodium Batteries instead. This does reduce their energy capacity though. Later on, Vibrant Alloy will make excellent tools with great durability. There are, however, a multitude of other great materials that you may have access to, so take a look around in NEI and decide for yourself.

There are also MV and HV versions, though they require that you can process Aluminium or Stainless Steel, respectively.

Black and Decker

But fear not, you can still find them in secret rooms on the first floor of some roguelike dungeons or ur-ghast towers. Better get searching...

allNodesLists.data: A Carbon crossbow limb is 1/3 the durability of the magnalium limb, but hits a lot harder and shoots a little faster. But you'll want to carry around a tinker table and extra ingots to repair it constantly, and watch that you don't break it in the middle of combat!

allNodesLists.name: Butane and Propane
allNodesLists.data:
You can crack and distill a lot of different fluids out of your already distilled products, such as Butane, Butene, Butadiene, Benzene, Ethane, Ethylene, Helium, Hydrogen, Methane, Octane, Propane, Propene, Toluene, and even more Light Fuel, Heavy Fuel, or Naphtha. You can then crack them down even further too sometimes. Many of these are only used for power. Go check out the spreadsheet for more details than this quest can encompass.

For now, get some Butane and Propane.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lButane and Propane
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Butane and Propane

allNodesLists.name: C9H8O4...NaCl...H2O...
allNodesLists.data:
Want to make some cetane-boosted diesel, plastic or some chemical dyes? Then it's time to craft a chemical reactor.

You can use the battery slot and the other extra slot in the GUI to store items.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lC9H8O4...NaCl...H2O...

allNodesLists.name: Cable Diodes
allNodesLists.data: Sometimes you just need a Diode, either to prevent burning up cables when splitting off a main line, or on a Thermos Server's chunk borders. Make one 4A Diode and get a 2A one for free!
allNodesLists.title: §5§lCable Diodes

allNodesLists.name: Cadmium
allNodesLists.data: You can get Cadmium from Sphalerite (centrifuge or thermal centrifuge). Later on you can use GT++ Ore processing chains to get Cadmium from Rare Earths. I don't care how you get it, just get some Cadmium.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lCadmium

allNodesLists.name: Cheaper Annealed Production
allNodesLists.data: It's even faster and cheaper to make annealed copper in the arc furnace than in the electric blast furnace. Annealed copper is a very good material for cables in MV. It only loses 1 EU per block.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lCheaper Annealed Production

allNodesLists.name: Chemical Bath
allNodesLists.data:
Wait, what? You want more byproducts from your ores? A cheaper way to make paper? Well, the chemical bath is perfect for you!

You'll have to provide liquids like mercury to extract different products like nickel, silver, copper, and platinum (only as PMP) from ores.

For paper you'll only need some water and wood pulp. Maybe you'll find more uses for it!
allNodesLists.title: §5§lChemical Bath
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Chemical Bath

You're Gonna Hate This #2

allNodesLists.name: Chemical Rubber Production
allNodesLists.data: A much more efficient way to make insulated cables is by making molten rubber in a chemical reactor, which can be applied to a cable in the assembling machine. When you put both machines next to each other you can output the molten rubber directly to the assembling machine by clicking the fluid auto-output button on the chemical reactor. Make sure to set the correct side of the reactor as output side by wrenching it. Also remember to use the right circuit in the assembling machine.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lChemical Rubber Production

allNodesLists.name: Chlorine, Your New Best Friend
allNodesLists.data:
Chlorine is a fluid that is used in significant quantities throughout the game, so you might as well get used to collecting it now.

You can electrolyse Salt, Rock Salt, Sodalite (finally a use!), or Salt Water for it. Since you'll need so much, you may wish to consider using your first Super Tank to hold it all.

allNodesLists.name: Choices, Choices
allNodesLists.data:
Need a map on fuel choices? Well, we don't have that, but we have suggestions. You can use Steam up to IV, but beyond MV it gets pretty painful.

In LV you can start refining oil for either Light Fuel for a Combustion Generator or Refinery Gas for a Gas Turbine. Or you can use Creosote in a Semi-Fluid Generator.

Once you hit MV, you can switch from Steam to renewable Benzene (Gas) from your logs. Other renewable alternatives are Fish Oil or Seed Oil based bio diesel (combustion). Seed Oil can be sourced from Pam's peanuts, IC2 Rape crop or Forestry tree nuts.

At MV you can also upgrade your Light Fuel with Heavy Fuel to get Diesel. When you reach HV turn diesel or bio diesel into Cetane Boosted Diesel. In EV, you can make High Octane Gasoline (HOG), but it's complex, and you'll need to rejigger your whole oil distillation setup, since it uses different fluids than Cetane does.

EV introduces the Large Gas Turbine, Large Steam Turbine, Large HP Steam Turbine, and Large Combustion Engine, which are more efficient versions of the earlier ones. The first 3 require turbines.

You can also make Nukes, or Wind and Water Kinetics.

For low-power operations, or dedicated players willing to setup autocrafting, you can begin using Solar Panels at MV.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lChoices, Choices

allNodesLists.name: Circuit Programming
allNodesLists.data:
Some machines have a very, very large number of recipes. To avoid conflicts, many recipes have programmed circuits to ensure that the correct recipe is used. These programmed circuits are not consumed.

In this modpack, all singleblock GT machines now come with an icon in the GUI on the bottom-right that represents a ghost circuit. Click it or scroll to choose the number you need. If you do that, you don't have to insert a physical circuit. This is going to be your main option for all single block machines. This option is now also available for input buses of multiblocks, which you will use much later.

There are a few places throughout the modpack where you still need the physical circuits. You can turn an LV circuit into a programmed circuit in the crafting grid and then program it in various ways:

1) Find a correct crafting recipe with a screwdriver in NEI and use that.

2) Right-click while holding the programmed circuit to open an easy menu. You still need to at least have the screwdriver in your inventory though or it won't work. Eventually you can also make an electric screwdriver.

3) Use the BartWorks Circuit Programmer. It's only available in MV, but it does not use any durability and runs on EU.

4) Use the GT++ Circuit Programmer block. It isn't portable and only available in MV, but it allows for automation.


The tasks in this quest are just the showcase of what programming circuits there are. You can just click the checkmark once you understand how the programmed circuits work.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lCircuit Programming

You can also just electrolyze it out in MV, which is what you §oshould§r be doing instead of this, but assuming you actually need it this method has higher yields (at the cost of carbon of course).

allNodesLists.name: Diamond Spikes
allNodesLists.data:
Diamond Spikes damages mobs (or you!) that touch any side of it other than the bottom. With 7 attack damage, the Spike does as much damage as a Diamond Sword. Mobs will not walk around the block, but will try to walk over it as if it were a regular solid block. Most explosions won't destroy the Spike because it has a very high blast resistance.

These can also be enchanted with all the enchantments a regular diamond sword would receive. This includes Looting and Sharpness, which function exactly as it does on a sword. Interestingly, mobs killed by the Diamond Spike will return experience as if killed by the player.

There are weaker versions, but who wants that? If you happen to want the last hit, you might want the wooden ones though.

allNodesLists.name: Diodes
allNodesLists.data:
Good circuits need diodes. There are two main ways to craft them. You can crush the Gallium Arsenide crystals to dust and combine that with fine copper wires and molten glass. Once you have solar grade silicon you can use it to make silicon wafers in your EBF to make even more. Note that the wafers are much more efficient on gallium and arsenic, so even a reduced amount is still worth it.

Make sure you check all the NEI recipes for advanced items instead of just using the first one you find. You can use annealed copper wires and polyethylene to increase your output even more.

allNodesLists.name: Enderman Smelterman
allNodesLists.data:
Need enderpearls? Getting them by killing endermen can be dangerous. Instead of doing that, put an enderman into a smeltery with hot fluids and use a gem cast to get guaranteed pearls.

The higher the hit points, the longer they'll last, so the more pearls you get. If you can find a regenerating enderman, or an enderman spawner, you'll have all the pearls you would ever want. Later on with EnderIO you can even create your own powered spawner to make endermen on-demand. Or just place it in the End and move the mobs inside.

Use a nametag on a regenerating enderman to make sure he doesn't despawn. You'll want to keep him from seeing the sky or else he'll teleport away.

If you haven't found a regen enderman yet, you can buy enderman spawn eggs to put into your smeltery with coins. Maybe you'll get lucky and get a regenerating one.

allNodesLists.name: Exploding Fluids For Power
allNodesLists.data:
The Combustion Generator produces EU from several fluids and spends fuel only when necessary. Some fluids are more popular than others, but the Oil processing line has a different combustion fluid in every tier from LV to EV, and all of them are burned in these generators.

To start, LV is the tier of Light Fuel. It is worth much more than the Oil itself for generating power, so you should distill and dessulfurize the Oil to get clean Light Fuel and use it for power. It's a great way to run your base, and can be upgraded further in the next tiers. Check the "Working with Oil" tab for more information, once you've made a Pump and found some Oil.

If you're dealing with Oil processing, this is the type of generator you'll use the most.§r

allNodesLists.data:
The fluid canner used to be the main way to fill cells, single-use batteries, and coolant cells. It was needed because direct interaction with cells was limited.

Now everything is much easier and cells almost always work as expected, so you likely won't need this, even for molten redstone.

Another interesting thing about this is it also works as a fluid uncanner. And maybe later you could fill a Lighter with it.

allNodesLists.name: Gallium Arsenide Crystal
allNodesLists.data:
The diode requires gallium arsenide, and you may be wondering how to get gallium or arsenic this early in the game.

Sphalerite and zinc are the primary sources of gallium at this tier.

You can find sphalerite in sulfur veins at Y 5-20, and the small zinc ores in the Overworld or the Nether at Y 80-210. You won't find much on the Overworld because of obvious reasons. To get additional zinc crushed ore drops, use a Tinker's Construct tool with the Luck (Fortune) enchant on it, probably the best use for all that lapis you got while looking for calcite. Or use a miner, if you don't mind how slow it is.

- Sphalerite can be electrolyzed for a small chance of a gallium dust. Better put in a lot or you might get unlucky.
- Zinc crushed ore can be washed and then thermal centrifuged or forge hammered and then centrifuged. But you don't always get the crushed ore as a drop, the impure dust doesn't give gallium.

You can get arsenic from realgar small ores in the Nether at Y 15-85. Centrifuge the dusts in a centrifuge.

Other sources are Tinker's Construct cobalt ore in the nether and cobaltite ore in the Twilight Forest. You can use your EBF for that. You also need to level up your pickaxe to ardite or make an Ironwood Pickaxe or LV Miner to harvest cobalt ore.

Another way to get gallium and arsenic is with XP buckets in a crafting grid if you're really desperate.

With your EBF you can combine these two dusts to make a Gallium Arsenide Crystal.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lGallium Arsenide Crystal

allNodesLists.name: Getting Ready for Tier 2, MV
allNodesLists.data:
In order to proceed forward, you need to get aluminium. A lot of it. But for now, 8 is enough to complete this quest.

Your first option is alumina dust. Probably the best source for alumina is clay or hardened clay from canyons, however you need an MV machine for that, so you need to find an alternative until you have enough dust for your initial setup. For now, you can get it by centrifuging various impure piles from your ores or by smelting ruby, sapphire, or green sapphire in an EBF with carbon. Check the EBF quest in the Multiblock Goals.

You will also need an EBF to turn the alumina into aluminium ingots. For that you need cryolite. Go visit the Twilight Forest for that and find a Cryolite vein. The related quest is "Lead, Galena, Silver and Cryolite" is the Novice Thaumaturgy tab.

Your second option is to use aluminium dust. However, you can not smelt that directly yet, even if you have an EBF. That will require higher heat levels. For now, you will have to either use a Tinker's Smeltery or a GT Compressor to turn the dust into raw aluminium which you can then smelt into ingots in the EBF. Check out the Tier 0 quest for some options to obtain the dust.

By the time you've completed this, you'll probably be done with most of the tab, but you'll still need Good Circuits (MV) to actually open up the next tier if you haven't done that yet.

You might also want to check the Getting Around and Without Dying tabs for new unlocks.

[note]If you were exploring Twilight Forest before 2.1.1.4 you won't find any cryolite in existing veins. You'll need to explore new chunks.[/note]

allNodesLists.name: Handle Tiny Piles Like a K1ng
allNodesLists.data:
Don't you hate having to manually compress all those tiny piles? Well, let me show you how to automate that. A combination of type filter, chest buffer (or super buffer in HV) and packager frees you from that annoying task. The chestbuffer can hold up to 9 stacks of tiny piles and the super buffer can hold 256 stacks of tiny dusts, which is more than enough. You can set its mode with a screwdriver on the output side. Set it to 9 to export 9 tiny piles at a time and let the packager compress these into regular dusts.

Super buffers can be lag sources, so be careful to keep them as empty as possible. If you're using a multiblock packager, be sure to change the buffer from Stocking mode to Transfer Size mode.

allNodesLists.name: Heavy Fuel
allNodesLists.data:
By adding Hydrogen to sulfuric Heavy Fuel in a Chemical Reactor you can produce Heavy Fuel, with a burn value of 240,000 EU per cell! Aside from this, it's also required for Diesel, in MV, which is a better fuel, and it can also be distilled into three very useful fluids: Benzene, Toluene and Phenol.

If you want to use Heavy Fuel as a power source, you will need Semi-Fluid generators, unlike Light Fuel and Diesel which use Combustion generators.

It's honestly not especially efficient to make Heavy Fuel out of regular Oil. You should try to get Heavy Oil to make it, like from Oilsands Ore in MV once you can. Then use it to make Diesel.

allNodesLists.name: Hello Baron, How's Your Black Gold Today?
allNodesLists.data:
During your travels you may have seen some huge oil spouts. Now's the time to make a pump and go collect this black gold into tanks. Oil can be burned directly in a combustion generator (onsite to power the pump, perhaps?) or be refined for better fuels and crafting materials.

Bring a generator or battery buffer (with full batteries obviously) with you to power the pump. Thanks to the advancement of technology the pump can auto output on top. Stacking multiple pumps makes them work faster. In that case, oil has to be removed from the bottom of the stack using a pump cover or other means like a conduit.

Taller spouts have more oil. But for the LV pump, it's better to use the short spouts if possible since it doesn't have enough range to fully collect the larger ones in the horizontal range. Save the taller spouts for MV or HV pumps.

Mining pipes are needed for pumping the oil, same as the auto miner. When it hits the bottom (or something in the way), if there's no fluid left to collect, it will start retracting the pipes. Same thing if you disable it with a soft mallet. You can also change the range with a screwdriver if there's a reason to do that, like collecting lava in a limited area faster.

These are GT machines, so remember to protect them (and their power sources!) from rain on all sides. And set a waypoint with JourneyMaps so you don't forget where you placed it!

[note]Once you run out of surface oil, you'll want to turn to:
1) Oilsands ore, though this is better suited for making heavy oil
2) Making oil from logs in a pyrolyze oven
4) Bacterial Vat (EV+)
5) Crops
6) Bees
7) Underground (UG) oil. Dimensions generally have a couple fluids that can be accessed with a multiblock version of the pump, available in MV+[/note]

[note]Heavy oil cannot be used until MV for anything except lubricant and burning in semifluid generator since it requires MV distillery.[/note]

allNodesLists.name: Here's Some Oil
allNodesLists.data:
[note]Here the oil questlines diverge into two tabs - part about getting every possible output is in the LV tab, part about the usefulness of oil is in the Working with Oil tab, this quest is part of the latter.[/note]

Welcome! This is the questline that shows the path through oil processing towards all the useful items and fluids that can be obtained from it. Working with this black liquid involves a lot of steps that range from LV (Low Voltage), all the way to IV (Insane Voltage), and outputs that are useful at those tiers and beyond.

Oil is useful both for generating power, and to automate a lot of chemicals that are important for progression. As you progress, you will be able to get more of it, and get it faster, as well as process it in new ways that improve on the setup that you were using before. It is not a required path for progression in the pack, but it is a very useful one, should you choose to follow it.

The best way to start working with oil is to extract it from the surface. Oil spouts are visible without having to dig down, and they can be interacted with by using a Pump placed above them, alongside a generator that feeds it some power. You can use some of the Oil to generate this power for now.

allNodesLists.name: H for Hydrogen... the Rest of the Alphabet is Too Complicated...
allNodesLists.data:
Centrifuge some brown or yellow limonite dust, or use an Electrolyser with water to get some hydrogen.

There are many other ways of obtaining hydrogen which you might want to look into. Some are only available much later.

Examples are: chemical processing or electrolysis of methane obtained from organic sources, electrolysis of water or salt water, mixing sodium with water, or eventually siphoning hydrogen directly from a gas giant.

allNodesLists.data:
Salt ore mixes can be found in the Overworld between Y 50-70.

Salt isn't only used to get sodium, it's an important ingredient in many pam's harvestcraft food recipes.

Lepidolite and spodumene are good sources of lithium for your batteries. Later on you can get a lot more in different ways.

allNodesLists.data:
Some centrifugal processes leave gases behind like Hydrogen or Methane. Centrifuge some Brown and Yellow Limonite to get Hydrogen or dump your unused food in a Centrifuge to get Methane gas. Wood will even give 60 mb per log, and many other crops will also generate Methane this way.

The main powergen line that uses this generator is Benzene, but that needs MV tier.

If you're dealing with fully renewable powergen, this is the type of generator you'll use the most.

allNodesLists.name: Keeping things organized
allNodesLists.data:
Are you tired of storing Shapes and/or Molds near your Extruders and Solidifiers instead of inside them? Today must be your lucky day, because these item holders let you do exactly that!

They allow your machines to hold a small number of extra items, though each slot can only store one item at a time. There are three versions of this cover, each offering a different amount of storage:

Good Item Holder: 12 slots

[note]If that's still not enough space and you are already using the highest tier, you can simply attach multiple holders to your machine of choice.[/note]

allNodesLists.data:
By adding Hydrogen to Sulfuric Light Fuel in a Chemical Reactor you can produce Light Fuel with the very high burn value of 305,000 EU per cell. It is also the main component of Diesel, an excellent fuel that becomes available in MV

The remaining Hydrogen Sulfide can be used to produce Sulfuric Acid for, well, tons of stuff. You can never have enough of it! You can also crack Light Fuel in a Chemical Reactor and then distill it to get Ethylene, for Polyethylene. But Refinery Gas is better for that.

allNodesLists.name: Long Distance Fluid Pipeline
allNodesLists.data:
Wouldn't it be great if you could transport your oil from a far away oil spout or oil field by pipes to your base?

This is not a problem anymore. Connect your setup on the start and end point with a Long Distance Fluid Pipeline block. Inbetween use the associated pipe blocks - the total distance between endpoints must be more than 64 blocks apart (4 or more chunks). There can only be one start and end point per pipeline.

To actually connect it, you need to align the start LDFP block such that the arrows are facing inwards, and the opposite side of it has a LDFPP block. Put a pump on the side of the block that has the arrows and set to import. It will now attempt to import fluid to the endpoint LDFP. §2This will go as fast as you can put fluid into it.§r

Do the opposite on the far side, except you don't need a pump.

Now you only need to chunkload the start and end points and the fluid will be "teleported" to you.

Of course, later on you'll probably use ender tanks to §oactually§r teleport the fluid, especially from other dims.

This setup is lag-free in the pipe blocks, so it's useful in your base as well if you want to reduce lag.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lLong Distance Fluid Pipeline
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Long Distance Fluid Pipeline
Prequest requests:
Hello Baron, How's Your Black Gold Today?

allNodesLists.name: Long Distance Item Pipeline
allNodesLists.data:
Wouldn't it be great if you could transport ores from a far away ore vein by pipes to your base?

This is not a problem anymore. Connect your setup on the start and end point with a Long Distance Item Pipeline block. Inbetween use the associated pipe blocks - the total distance between endpoints must be more than 64 blocks apart (4 or more chunks). There can only be one start and end point per pipeline.

To actually connect it, you need to align the start LDIP block such that the arrows are facing inwards, and the opposite side of it has a LDIPP block. Put a conveyor on the side of the block that has the arrows and set to import. It will now attempt to import stuff to the endpoint LDIP. This will go as fast as you can put items into it.§r

Do the opposite on the far side, except you don't need a conveyor.

Now you only need to chunkload the start and end points and the items will be "teleported" to you.

Of course, later on you'll probably use ender chests to §oactually§r teleport the ore, especially from other dims.

This setup is lag-free in the pipe blocks, so it's useful in your base as well if you want to reduce lag.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lLong Distance Item Pipeline

allNodesLists.name: Lossless LV Cables
allNodesLists.data:
How about lossless 32 EU cables? Redstone alloy is a superconductor and will transfer your energy without any loss.

Redstone Alloy is a new alloy which requires an EBF. Mix redstone, silicon and coal by hand, or in the mixer for a better result.

[note]Remember not to mix it up with Red Alloy, that's the ULV one.[/note]
allNodesLists.title: §5§lLossless LV Cables

allNodesLists.name: LPG
allNodesLists.data: Centrifuging Butane or Propane gives you LPG with a burn value of 320,000 EU, the same as naphtha.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lLPG

allNodesLists.name: Lubricant​
allNodesLists.data:
Using lubricant instead of water or distilled water in your cutting machines will increase their speed.

You can make lubricant out of oil, seed oil, fish oil or creosote in a distillery (or distillation tower later on). If you're able to craft a brewery you can use talc or soapstone to get much more lubricant each cycle.

Lube cells are required to make low tier energy hatches, so stockpile a few cells and use the rest to make your cutting machine faster.

Lubricant​

allNodesLists.data: The LV GT++ Steam Boiler is the next machine you can build to produce steam more efficiently than with the High Pressure Boiler. It won't use fuel up unless it starts to run low on steam, so it's very efficient.

LV Advanced Steam Boiler

A Lead About Lead That Leads to Lead

allNodesLists.name: LV Extruder
allNodesLists.data: The extruder is not very useful in LV. But it will extrude your next tier of boat, make rubber sheets more efficiently, get you extra fluid cells, or make §osome§r Tinkers Construct tool parts.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lLV Extruder

allNodesLists.name: Machine Interface Fluid I/O
allNodesLists.data:
Thanks to the tireless work of the devs, you can now use cells to I/O fluids directly from the interface of GT machines. Just click on the fluid while holding a cell or other fluid container item.

Points to consider:
1) Left click to attempt filling/emptying all fluid containers held on cursor.
2) Right click to attempt filling/emptying one fluid container held on cursor.
3) All fluid containers that can be used in a standard gt tank (e.g. super tanks or the X voltage tanks) are supported, including but not limited to: water bottles, vanilla buckets, ic2 (universal and normal) cells, volumetric flasks, large fluid cells, pressurized fluid tanks, etc.
4) Can fill/take less than one cell (1000L or 144L if molten) of fluid if the fluid container supports doing so.
5) It won't check if it's a valid fluid for the machine/recipe, keep that in mind.
6) Doesn't work with Crops++ alcohols, feel free to code compatibility for us.
7) EIO tanks need to be placed and picked up first before they can be used.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lMachine Interface Fluid I/O
allNodesLists.tooltip:
Machine Interface Fluid I/O

Welcome to Tier 1, LV

allNodesLists.name: Magnalium Crossbow Bolts
allNodesLists.data:
Magnalium bolts are much better than your old wooden bolts.

You can use nether quartz on the bolts to make them even better. This requires a free modifier slot.

Experiment with NEI to find other good bolt materials.

To make these bolts, you must use a Fluid Solidifer instead of the Tinker's casting table. It's important that you get the molten iron out of the smeltery and into the Fluid Solidifier, the GT molten iron won't work.

The bolts should be in your inventory if you want to pick up the ones you fired. You can't pick them up if the bolts are in Battlegear slots.

Magnesite, the source of Magnesium can be found in the Twilight Forest at Y 10-40. Fullers Earth can be found on the Overworld at Y 50-70. Marble dust is a great source of Magnesium too.
Other options in LV are Pyrope, Olivine, or Ashes.

allNodesLists.name: Magnets != Magic
allNodesLists.data:
Tired of running after ore or other blocks? Use a magnet! It has a limited range, but who cares? Just remember to turn it on.

In HV you can craft it into the better one, if you still need a magnet by then.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lMagnets != Magic

allNodesLists.data: Mercury can be centrifuged out of redstone. If you find some cinnabar ore in a redstone vein or one of the infused stone veins you can use that too.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lMercury

allNodesLists.name: Methane
allNodesLists.data:
Distilling some "refinery gases" gives you some methane gas. There are many more (and probably better) ways to get methane.

You will need this in later tiers, for PTFE as an example.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lMethane

allNodesLists.name: Mica Ore
allNodesLists.data: Mica is a very rare but useful ore. You need it in order to craft your coils for the Electric Blast Furnace. Only for cupronickel coils there is a replacement recipe. If you have no luck in finding this vein yet try to look for it with a Prospector once you get them.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lMica Ore

allNodesLists.name: Mjolnir!!!
allNodesLists.data:
Not really required, but it is a lot faster than the steam one and it can be automated. If you feel like ore washing is too slow, use this hammer.

[note]You can also consider using the steam multiblock instead if you want.[/note]
allNodesLists.title: §5§lMjolnir!!!

allNodesLists.name: Molten Redstone?
allNodesLists.data:
You heard that the carpenter needs some molten redstone for a few recipes. Converting redstone dust into a fluid requires a fluid extractor. Let's build one.

If you want to get that molten redstone into a cell, you'll need a fluid canner instead of a GT tank. Why? Because Reasons.

Fortunately, most fluids work properly, but redstone, cracked fluids, and certain other ones do not. Or just use a universal cell.
allNodesLists.title: §5§lMolten Redstone?

allNodesLists.name: Naphtha
allNodesLists.data:
You can process Sulfuric Naphtha to fluid Naphtha which has a burn value of 220,000 EU in the Gas Turbine. Naphtha can be used to get Ethylene for Polyethylene, but it shares this use with Refinery Gas and Light Fuel, so decide for yourself which one you want to use.

If you choose to make High-Octane Gasoline in EV and onwards, it will need a lot of Naphtha. You can also make Polycaprolactam (Nylon), which doesn't have any useful purpose yet, but it might get some in the near future.

You can get some nitrogen by centrifuging... air. This process takes a long time, especially at LV tier.

You get that air from compressed air cells, which are gotten from running cells through a compressor. Each one contains 2000L, unlike a normal cell that contains 1000L.

allNodesLists.name: Node Upgrades
allNodesLists.data:
Nodes can take many upgrades. For now, try building a World Interaction Upgrade. With it, you can setup simple autocrafting.

Put a WIU in a transfer node attached to a crafting table. On the other side of the table, the 3x3 area is now treated as a crafting grid. Place items in inventories on the other side and if they make a valid recipe, the WIU will craft it. To speed it up, you will need to wait until HV for stainless steel.

Also, if you place a node on a block of cobble that has lava and water next to it, and a WIU in it, it will produce cobble for you automatically. Use upgrades to get more at a time and faster.

[warn]The WIU can NOT be used for infinite water in GTNH.[/warn]
allNodesLists.title: §5§lNode Upgrades

allNodesLists.data: Why waste a full ingot to make a rod by using a tool which loses durability and takes even MORE ingots? With this little device, all your rod-needs shall be fulfilled (for now at least, the MV Extruder is the next step for rods).
